Review Title: Just amazing. There flights and service are outstanding.
Review Text:
These guys were amazing.
From the customer service to the actual tour, these guys just had it going on.
As the 1st day in Talkeetna was overcast and snowing, we rebooked our flight to our last day in Talkeetna. The team were very helpful in this.
As we had finished a dog mushing tour on our second day, the weather was superb and you could see the 3 mountains from town.
Luckily for us, we walked to airport and asked if we could get on the flight from our rebooked ticket the next day and they managed to get us on the flight that day. The team at the airport base were super helpful in this.
The flight was amazing. We were lucky enough to see all three mountains in the one flight and the scenery was spectacular. Its hard to put into words. The only issue we had was another companies plane was on the glacier runway and we couldn't land. Our pilot Jack tried to wait a few minutes and took a quick lap around the area to come back and see if we could get down but it wasn't safe so we couldn't land and then we flew back to base. When talking to the team at the airport, we said we had an amazing experience and a shame we missed the landing. You don't have to pay for that part as well if you didn't get it. As we were buying some merchandise from the shop, the staff came back to us and asked us if we wanted to jump on the next flight, for free, and only pay for the landing if we got it. We jumped at the chance. We got the same pilot Jack again for our next flight. He was excellent and explained and answers for questions when asked over the radio. Luckily, we got a glacier landing on this flight.
It was an amazing experience and well worth the money. Luckily for us we got two flights for the price of the one.
I cant thank the team at K2 aviation for the help they gave us. There customer service was amazing, just like the service they provide.
I would thoroughly recommend K2 aviation for a Denali flight experience. Its a must do when in Talkeetna

Review Title: Do the Glacier Landing, it’s the best part of the tour!
Review Text:
Great experience with K2! This was a once in a lifetime experience for my daughter and I; it was everything we expected and more. The line was long when we arrived but they were fully staffed to meet demand and we were checked in quickly. After checking in we were on the flight within 10 minutes. The pilot was very knowledgeable and easy going. We got some great pictures from the flight and glacier landing.

If you are going to take the tour, I highly recommend the Glacier Landing. It’s more expensive but it really was the highlight of our flight (with the exception of seeing Mt. Denali of course).

Every seat is good in the plane so no need to rush on it to get the best seat. Also we sat in the last two rows since we were the last onboard and we enjoyed have a lot of leg room compared to the other seats.

Some advice for first time flyers specifically re: Glacier Landings:

1. Bring a jacket even if it’s 80 degrees in Talkeetna since the weather changes so much in the mountains. Wear layers if you only have a thin coat. I had a t-shirt and windbreaker but I wish I had something warmer since it was chilly on the glacier during our late evening flight.

2. Wear the boot covers they give you at K2. They keep your shoes dry during the glacier landing!! I was surprised how many folks on our flight did not wear them.

3. Make sure you take lots of photos! Bring an extra camera if you have it. The views are stunning!

I would definitely fly with K2 aviation again!

Review Text: This is a very popular service offering Air Taxis and flight tours. We booked the Denali flight tour to fly around Mt Denali, see wildlife and land on a glacier and actually walk on the glacier. What they don't tell you is that none of their pilots are instrument certified and can only fly by visual flight rules which means if it's rainy, foggy or has a lot of low clouds your trip will be canceled or greatly shortened. Our trip was shortened and we didn't get to se or do most of the highlights of the trip. We spent 15 minutes getting to the mountain and 15 minutes getting back and actually flew around the mountain for 30 minutes. No glacier landing and didn't spot a single bear, moose or any type of wildlife. We also didn't know how far it was from Fairbanks when we booked the tour, but that was our fault for not asking. We assumed the tour would start and end around or near Denali but after purchasing the package learned that we'd have to drive almost to Anchorage (way past the mountain)  take the tour and fly back almost to Anchorage and then drive back to Fairbanks. So it ended up being a 12 hour day for a 30 minute to 1 hour tour. We had also been told we had to each purchase a park pass in advance before taking the tour and we did, but we never needed it because we never landed inside the park. Once back home I called the tour operator (K2 Aviation) and complained to the owner, who after considering the facts agreed to give us a partial refund which I did appreciate.

Review Text: In all our research for Alaska, what stood out the most was the encouragement to see Alaska from as many perspectives as we could - land, sea, air. When we figured out that flightseeing out of Talkeetna would not only work great for our schedule, but allow us to experience the Alaska Range and Mount Denali, it wasn't a hard choice to go with K2 Aviation. The reviews were overwhelmingly positive, and we really appreciated the transparency on their website for the different routes available. From booking, to arrival, and check-in, the staff was very kind and helpful. I tend to be a bit of a nervous flyer ever since experiencing a super bumpy ride many years ago in a small 2 seater plane, but Lauren in the office was so encouraging and genuine in putting my mind at ease. We had booked the Denali Grand Tour, but due to weather conditions up there, we weren't going to be able to fly that route. Instead, we were offered the Denali Flyer and a refund for the price difference. For anyone wondering if a certain time of day is best, there really isn't, and all the staff confirmed this. Whatever time works best for you, is the best time to go! We were there for a 6:30 PM and it was an absolutely beautiful, sunny and clear day - and yet we still had changes because the cloud and/or wind conditions are always going to be completely different higher up and around the mountains. We had an absolutely fantastic time, and I felt great throughout the flight! I do recommend being on Dramamine or Bonine if you're prone to motion sickness and/or have some anxiety with flying - take one dose the night before to metabolize in your system, and one prior to your activity. Being prepared is key! Our pilot Mitch was very friendly, professional, and knowledgeable about anything and everything we saw from the air. The views were breathtaking, and we learned so much! It was an almost out of this world experience to feel like you're floating above and among the mountains. We were prepared to do a glacier landing, but some last minute cloud cover interfered. It was still an awesome experience though, and one we won't soon forget!

Review Title: Don’t fly on an overcast day
Review Text:
I don’t usually write reviews but K2 has sent me several emails asking for one and I searched for this info before our trip and didn’t really find anything. The weeks leading up to our trip bad weather was in the forecast. Now I know not to trust a forecast until you get close to the date and Denali is a big place and had different weather throughout. Apparently K2 hadn’t flown in weeks. I feel for them this is a tough business with Covid and the weather not to be able to generate revenue. I wasn’t sure what their weather policy was so I emailed them and got this response:

“The weather in Alaska is highly variable, and many factors do influence our ability to fly. We can fly in rain as long as visibility permits and the weather is conducive up in the mountain range, but we always prioritize safety. Our decision for your flight will be made right around your check-in time, as it allows us to use the most accurate weather updates and best predict the flight conditions”

Visibility and conditions were quickly dropping before our flight. We had booked the glacier landing and were told we could still go but the pilot would make the decision in the air for the landing or not. As soon as we were in the air it was clear we wouldn’t be landing. The flight was still an experience but visibility was terrible and my partner got sick due to the bumpiness and another passenger spent the entire flight hunched over. I believe we were the last flight of the day they allowed to take off.

I’ve heard from several other people if you can land on the glacier it is a once in a lifetime magical experience. I wouldn’t recommend going up in lower visibility or poor conditions. All the photos and videos you see from K2 are in perfect conditions. Which 100% look worth it but I wouldn’t pay the price again for a low visibility bumpy flight. They did promptly refund us the difference for not being able to do the glacier landing and only charged us for a regular flight tour.

Review Text:
On two other trips to Alaska I have booked with K2 and had the flights cancelled due to weather. Please note that this was no problem for me. They are not going to fly if it is unsafe or they cannot provide you the experience you are paying for. The money was promptly refunded.

On this trip we arrived in Talkeetna without a tour reservation. As we drove in, I heard the planes taking off from the local airport. I immediately rounded up the family and headed over to see if we could get on a flight. It was no problem and 45 minutes later we were boarding a late afternoon tour.

I believe we were on the Denali Flyer. My sense is the routes are a generalization of length and the areas they will try to show you. I felt like the pilot adjusted the flight based on where things were clear and we could get the best views/experience for the time we had in the air. It is unsafe and pointless to follow a route that is cloud-covered. It was a great tour and I thought the pilot did an excellent job of allowing both sides of the plane to see the different sites. He was informative about the area and things we were seeing. This was the first activity we did in Alaska and set a great tone for the rest of the trip. The family absolutely loved it. We did not have the choice of a glacier landing due to the uncertain weather, so I cannot comment on whether that is a worthwhile addition. I can say that, although expensive, you are not getting the most out of your Alaska trip without some flight seeing. There is just too much of Alaska that is inaccessible from the ground. You need to get into the air to truly get the full experience. Highly recommend K2...take any trip you can afford. If you have the option, I would take a cheaper trip and save money for a second trip of another kind...there is so much to see in this state.

Review Text:
DISCLAIMER: I’m a tour professional living and working here in Alaska and not compensated in any way for this review. I do it because these operators are my FELLOW ALASKANS.

There are a handful of memory-making travel experiences around the world that are worth the extra expense after just “getting there”. When you come to South Central Alaska (the greater Anchorage area), a flight up into the Alaska Range is a must. Sure, it’s spendy. (But many worthwhile things in life aren’t easy or cheap.) Get a mountain-sized dose of amazement and humility flying among the mountains above glacier-covered gorges. The beauty is mesmerizing. Feeling so tiny against these giant peaks gives one the opportunity to take a breath and view life's hassles with a little humility and perspective.

I’ve been bringing guests to K2 Aviation for almost two decades because of their outstanding commitment to safety and hospitality. From nearly immaculate aircraft to the thoughtful considerations like a basket of “loaner” sunglasses, K2 has this thing figured out! With K2, everything from the patience of the folks on the phones explaining prices and weather, to the shuttle drivers and pilots who clearly LOVE what they do, these people care that guests have a genuinely amazing time. But it’s not just tour groups that get great service. I’ve seen independent travelers in rental cars walk away after a flight with the same joyful glow that my guests get after a great flight.

REAL TALK: The Alaska Range is tricky. The weather up here is tricky. Book the first available time slot that you can. Try to be in Talkeetna more than one night to increase your chances of a “try again” flight in case weather isn’t cooperative during your visit. What K2 tells you about weather and visibility comes from a deep tradition of transparency with their guests. They really desire that everyone has a great flight. They have been forthright with me in communication. I trust them when they advise me about weather and I know from years of successful flights and hundreds of happy clients that they want all fliers to come away with a mind-blowing, life-changing flight in the Alaska Range!

TIPS: Be on time. Wear a mask. Tip your pilot. If you’re in a group, one person takes a time-lapse video and others take photos to share later. Put down the cameras every few minutes and soak in the experience with your eyes and your imagination. Enjoy the moment and make some truly amazing memories!

Review Title: Flight Seeing of Denali from Talkeetna
Review Text: On a trip to Alaska for a family wedding, we decided to spend extended time in the state exploring Talkeetna and Denali National Park.  We opted for a flight seeing excursion from Talkeetna to see Denali rather than a lengthy 10 hour bus trip within the National park as we had heard bus trippers made the effort but never saw Denali (even tho weather was clear earlier in the day). Made reservation with K2 several days before so we knew the forecast.  Our pilot, Chad, gave each side of the plane many opportunities to view Denali plus offered comments regarding climbers’ base camps, named glaciers, blue glacier pools, ski tracks from climbers, etc. Our flight landed on Ruth Glacier and allowed about 20 minutes to get out of the plane and walk on the glacier.  We took hundreds of photos as the day was clear with few clouds.  Although we dressed for warmth for higher elevations (thermal ski clothes liners), Chad was wearing a short sleeved Hawaiian shirt so needless to say, he expected fabulous weather which is exactly what we got.  Sunglasses were a must!  The biggest thrill for me was that I was allowed to sit in copilot seat on return to Talkeetna and able to video takeoff from glacier curving up and thru a canyon to save and re-experience this once in a lifetime event. Definitely a highlight of our Alaskan adventure!

Now that we had lost the opportunity to see Anchorage as originally planned, we did the yellow tour. I understand weather condition can change - the green tour may not be running in morning but might run at our scheduled time. But when we explicitly asked if green tour was running - they should have told us honestly. Instead they were telling us it is 'fully booked'.

Had they honestly told us that green one was not running since morning, we would have not skipped seeing Anchorage for the 'possibility' of green tour . It was because of their false confirmation that green one is running, we changed our itinerary.

Review Text:
I don’t think I can find the words to explain how much I loved my experience with K2 but here goes nothing.

We took off (me and four other passengers) with Chris as our pilot in the DHC - 2 Beaver at 13:00 on Sunday, the 11th of October of 2020 when it was partly overcast with 2-5 mph winds, no precipitation and a low of 37° F. I was lucky, because the weather cleared up even more so while we were in the air and it gave us a great view of the peak of Denali. Despite losing a game of Rock Paper Scissors with another passenger over who gets shotgun, it was the most comfortable and smoothest flight I’ve ever been on (yes even including the 10s of commercial airlines I have flown over the course of my life). Our pilot, Chris, is a wonderful person and a very humble pilot. Before we took off, he mentioned how the sound of the engine starting was like music to his ears, and I immediately knew I was in good hands. He is also incredibly knowledgeable about the geography, geology, and history of the park and Talkeetna area. Needless to say he is the best pilot / tour guide anyone could ask for. As for the views... The formations on the bedrock were outer-worldly, the Alaskan range looked vast and endless, the snow-kissed walls of the mountains were seemingly arms length away yet sensing the scale of such vistas became elusive, and the Kahiltna glacier became a grand pass over which our plane maneuvered and our eyes followed until we eventually landed on a bed of snow below. It was all phenomenal. However, you would just have to see it for yourself; words and photos don’t do much justice. After we landed on the glacier, we stood out on the range with a magnificent view of the Denali and it’s younger siblings and Chris suggested we take a moment to enjoy the quiet stillness of the environment which spurred a moment of pause that I think many of us could use. I got shotgun on the way back and the views were as incredible as the way in, with more unique views of the park. After landing back in talkeetna, I stepped off the plane with a newfound appreciation of our planet, Alaska, and it’s seemingly infinite wonders. I also never realized flying is so fun! All-in-all, I am very grateful for the kind and hardworking people at K2, their awesome aircrafts, and for giving me the gift of a unique experience I will never forget.

Best wishes,
Cez

Review Title: Words cannot describe how awesome this is!
Review Text:
I've been to Talkeetna a number of times. It's always been overcast or rainy, and I've loved it anyway, even when I haven't been fortunate to see Denali. This time was incredible, and K2 aviation, and our pilot Chris, put our trip over the top. Literally.

We'd been hesitant to do a Denali flight as it's so expensive. And the weather is so variable, we were afraid to commit. But after reading a number of reviews, it seemed worth doing if the weather seemed promising. We booked for one day, it turned out to be really hazy because of fires in Siberia (!) and K2 was great about allowing us to switch days. Chris our pilot was phenomenal from the second we met him. Incredibly knowledgeable, personable and professional. The weather was clear, and we saw Denali and other mountains, SO close up. We did a glacier landing, and at one point our family and Chris were the only ones on the ice field. It was like being in a dream.

This is an expensive trip. It is dependent on weather and other factors, and we know we were very lucky. But K2 is so professional, and with pilots like Chris, really maximize the potential that this will be an unforgettable experience. If you are able to be flexible with the timing that helps, because the weather changes so much.

Also, just have to say that we were nervous given Covid. But again, K2 was extremely professional, had exceptional hygiene practices both in and out of the aircraft, and I would not Covid concerns stop you from doing this trip.

Absolutely one of the top highlights of my recent trip to Alaska. We had signed up for the glacier landing and at check in were told that it was going to be too foggy to land. Once up in the air, our terrific pilot, Chris, had been eying the potential glacier landing field and decided that the conditions were much better than earlier and fog had cleared enough for a safe landing under the premise that we would need to be ready to leave should he sense the conditions changing once on the ground. Standing on the glacier in complete silence listening to rocks falling, glacial water rushing, was one of the most surreal experiences ever. Would 100% recommend this trip and the landing is absolutely worth it. Honorable mention to the way that the bright red plane pops on the white snow in all of our amazing pictures. Thanks, Chris and K2 aviation for the unforgettable experience!

Also, for anyone traveling in the current pandemic climate, K2’s COVID procedures felt very safe and clean and I feel they are doing a great job putting safety first.

Review Text:
We were told when we arrived at K2's very nice facility at the Talkeetna airport that due to weather our tour would be scaled back from the trip that circled Mt Denali and landed on a glacier, to a flight plan that just covered the lower mountains. And the price was adjusted to suit with our deposit covering the shorter flight of a little over an hour. K2 also offered a full refund. Since we had driven some two hours from Anchorage we decided to do what we could and take the shorter flight.

The thing to keep in mind is that the flight time to the edge of the park is 15-20 minutes one way. The pilot kept that interesting with discussions of rivers, the fall colors, and travel where there are no roads. Still, the travel to/from Denali is over flat terrain and is not very dramatic; only about half the total flight time was over the mountains and glaciers.

The weather was indeed cloudy at the park and the caution was appropriate because the pilot is flying visually. We caught a couple of long range views of Denali through the clouds, and we saw a number of glaciers that the pilot ably described. It was interesting and fun, may be not thrilling like we hoped, hence the 'three' rating. To their credit, K2 had provided email warnings about the weather conditions.

We were in the plane with a couple with a toddler who literally screamed the entire flight. This was not a problem, for us, because we had earphones. The parents were very distracted with the child so not sure the flight was a good idea for them.

About halfway thru the flight my wife's seat came un-pinned from its mount and we had about five exciting minutes locating the pin and doing an in-flight repair.

Overall, K2 did a good job; the pilot was a good guide as well as an experienced aviator. Given the travel time consideration it would be worth it to sign up for longer flights to get more out of the experience, with the understanding that the plan is ultimately determined by the weather.

Review Text:
My wife and I booked the Denali Experience with Glacier Landing for August 29.

K2 arranged pick-up and drop off service for us at the Talkeetna Lodge. The transfers were completed smoothly. We were informed that since Alaska experienced one of the warmest summers on records the snow on Denali was too soft to conduct the glacier landing. I had been following the latest Tripadvisor reviews and anticipated this situation, disappointing, but totally understandable. Since the tour was prepaid our credit card was reimbursed in a timely manner.

The plane has a capacity of 10 or 11 passengers and we had seven clients on this trip. You are provided with headphones which permit the pilot to narrate information during the flight. The headphones also contained a microphone which allows you to ask questions during the experience.

Each customers has a window seat which provides excellent views and an opportunity for unobstructed photography. Frequently the pilot would maneuver the plane so the passengers on the right side would have a view of a glacier/mountain/point of interest and then adjust the route so the passengers on the left side would have a similar view.

Due to the Swan Lake fire the visibility directly after take-off was less than ideal. The pilot indicated this would clear up as we gained altitude and approached the mountain range. He was 100% correct as visibility was excellent as we approached Denali.

The day before we were fortunate to observe Denali as we exited the park. K2 provided an entirely different visual experience. The excursion is definitely on the expensive side, but since this was likely our one and only trip to Alaska it was totally worth it.

The Denali Experience is the basic of the three tours that K2 offers, for us the length of time in the air was satisfactory.

Booked this with my father who was up in Alaska visiting me. The booking was pricey, especially when an entire 185 could have been chartered for the same money (and we'd have had seats to spare), but being able to land on the glacier was worth it, we thought.

When we arrived we learned the glacier landing was scrubbed due to the warm weather. Not much to be done about that-- we were disappointed but in no way upset about K2 for it. And besides, the weather was as clear and sunny as I have ever seen Denali, and smoke from the local wildfires had shifted out of the area, setting up K2 with the opportunity to give an absolutely amazing trip.

Instead, they blew it. We were ushered not to an Otter but a Piper Navajo, whose twin engines and low wings make it utterly horrible for a flight seeing plane-- probably why neither Talkeetna Air Taxi nor Sheldon Air Service across the taxiway from K2 have anything like it in their fleet. It is, however, a bit cheaper to operate than an Otterof which there were about 4 on the ramp at K2 when we departed. The picture attached shows the view out my window. I spent the entire flight with them obstructing the views and making pictures more difficult.

I won't be bringing any other visitors back to K2. Taking a scenic around Denali is certainly an experience, but K2 absolutely blew it. I'll be taking future visitors elsewhere.

The professionalism that our pilot and ground service (rampers) showed was wonderful. We had an older gentleman that urinated on himself during the last half of the flight. The gentleman was on the last row and was first to get off. He told the pilot and ground crew that he had an accident. As any of us could imagine this had to be terribly embarrassing for the gentlemen. The pilot and ground crew stayed professional and never made any negative comments. The pilot made sure attention was taken off of the man. They all should get a pat on the back. Everyone from registration people to the other pilots were very friendly!

Now, the flight was unbelievable! Many things you do once in a life but this is something we would do again! The summit tour was breathtaking. Our pilot made sure we were comfortable. He checked with us regularly for cabin temps, ears on decent etc. We all had a window seat. So, basically there is no bad seat. Everyone gets an equal chance to see. The only thing we would have done differently was add the glacier landing. At the time we went glacier landings was not safe because there was not enough snowfall during the night. Facilities were great! Coffee, tea and hot chocolate provided. The only thing you need is a pair of sunglasses and your camera!

We highly recommend this flight for any age!

Review Text:
I got a wild idea and managed to talk my wife into a flight seeing excursion. We had looked at doing it while staying in Denali, but had heard that the rates were better out of Talkeetna and this would also give my wife (prone to motion sickness) a chance to let the scopolamine do its thing.

We had our tour guide book the excursion. We weren't really into landing on a glacier, but we wanted to see the summit of Denali. K2 had us booked in an older, but well-maintained Piper Navajo. Our pilot, Chad, went over all the safety briefings thoroughly. Even pointed out that there was survival gear in the back of the aircraft as well as a satellite phone.

We lifted off and were on our way. Since we would be around the summit of Denali and the aircraft is not pressurized, we had to don oxygen masks. This was everything I hoped for as I looked at my wife and said, "Talk to me, Goose."

The scenery is unparalleled. The rugged peaks of the Alaska Range are all around as you see glaciers, ice falls, and even the various climber camps. Chad took us around the area several times, gradually gaining altitude until we reached approximately 23,000 feet, about 2 miles from the summit. I looked around and pretty much everyone else just had this look of awe and wonder on their face. It's certainly a view you will never get from the ground.

I can't recommend this trip enough. All too soon, we headed back to a smooth landing at Talkeetna Airport and we were left with memories.

Review Title: Incredible views of mountains (Denali) and glaciers
Review Text:
My family really wanted to go on a flight-seeing tour and land on a glacier, so we started searching for them while in Anchorage. We found several great options, but ended up going with K2 Aviation since their availability best matched our schedule. We chose the Denali Flyer Tour because we wanted to see multiple sides of Denali but didn't think the Grand Denali was quite worth the added cost.

We arrived really early since the drive from Denali to Talkeetna took less time than we anticipated. We hung out in the parking lot and on the picnic benches in front of K2. They provide water, tea, etc.There was also WiFi for guests but it didn't work for me.

We checked in 30-45 minutes before our flight. Each person weights themselves with everything they're taking onto the plane. You can also borrow sunglasses at this time if you need. They have a great selection with all sorts of styles and sizes. We also got our overboots at this time.

About 10 minutes before our flight, the pilot called us over and gave us a safety briefing. Then, we got on the plane. He took volunteers for co-pilot and everyone else sat wherever they wanted. Every seat has a headset and a window. The headset is a bit uncomfortable since it really closes in on your ears and head.

The flight itself was incredible! We flew over the park and soared through the mountains. Our pilot pointed out all the major landmarks from the summits to glaciers. He didn't provide much information besides that, which was fine with me. He did a good job of showing Denali to both sides of the plane so everyone was able to get photos.

Near the end of the flight, we landed on Ruth Glacier. It was more like a field of snow than glacier ice, which was a little disappointing, but still a beautiful place. We had about 15 minutes on the glacier and then we got back on the plane and headed back.

Oh! One thing to note, it was rather hot when we were in Denali (highs of 75-80). It was also warm on the glacier and basically everyone wore short sleeves and jeans or shorts. No gloves, beanies, jackets, etc. were necessary.

Overall, I would recommend the flight to folks considering it. I wouldn't say it was the highlight of my trip, but it was definitely up there!

Review Title: Was Great Experience, but there was a BIG safety concern
Review Text:
We had booked "Denali Flyer Tour with Glacier Landing". Glacier landing was the best. And "Denali Flyer" was good enough in terms of the length and the time of the tour. I wouldn't opt for for the other 3 tours. This is good enough.

Our tour was scheduled to start at 3:00 pm. We were a family of 6. We did a checkin at 2:30 pm. Be there 30 mins prior to boarding. There is a restroom at the office, clean. If you forget to get your sun glasses, no worries, the staff there are helpful and you can borrow sun glasses, and return them after the flight. You get to borrow the boots kind that you wear on top of your shoes. So keep in mind, you don't need to bring your boots. Just the regular shoes that you are wearing for your entire trip is good enough. You pick your size from their storage box, wear them, meet the pilot when called around 15 mins prior to flying. The pilot walks you to the 10 seater plane and you get seated.

You wear your headset.
FEEDBACK:
1. MY HEADSET WAS NOT CONNECTED TO THE SOCKET. AFTER FEW MINTS I HAD TO FIGURE OUT
2. THE WORST PART WAS: I WAS SITTING NEXT TO THE ENTRY DOOR AND THE FLIGHT STARTS MOVING, AND I'M SHOCKED THE DOOR IS NOT CLOSED. I REMOVED MY SEAT BELT AND RAN TO THE PILOT AND TAPPED ON HIS SHOULDER AND TOLD HIM THE DOOR IS NOT CLOSED. HE STOPPED THE PLANE AND CAME AND CLOSED/LOCKED THE DOOR.

That was terrible terrible mistake of the pilot not having a checklist. Had I taken a minute or more to inform the pilot, maybe we all wouldn't have been in the plane to even tell. I as a passenger don't know how to close and lock that plane door, and for sure I don't want to do it myself and feel safe.

Then we go over the mountain, which was beautiful to see the snow tip from areal view. Then we land on a 4000 ft glacier surrounded by snow mountains. It was "nature at it's best".. just gorgeous. Absolute beauty. Amazing. We get to spend more than 20 mins and then fly back. The pilot was a good narrator. We land back. Return our sun glasses, boots, and back to our car.

Oh, Talkeetna was cute little town, we had Ice Cream and coffee. Should try it. It was great. And there are lot of Thai Restaurants if that's a point to keep in mind

Review Text: Wow.  Where do I begin. April 24 was a glorious day, and we had been anticipating a great adventure flying among the peaks and landing on a glacier.  The meticulously clean DeHaviland DHC-3 Otter was our bird and Chris was our pilot.  My husband and I were two of only three passengers on the plane, and the mountain peaks, the craggy cliffs we saw  and the glacier we landed on (Pika Glacier) -- Everything Was So Incredible!!   What was super special was that Chris would explain everything he knew about what we were seeing (and he knows a LOT!).  All of it was so interesting -- we both want to return for another flight in the spring or summer when the snow in the lower elevations has melted and the green has "returned" -- and we will ask for Chris to take us on yet another flight.  He's a great guy who is meticulous with everything (EVERYthing) he does, and we want more of his stories!!  Thanks, K2, for the amazing experience (I still think you should have a "Frequent Flyer" card... 6 flights and the 7th is free... or something like that.  I'd be game!).

Review Text:

We went out to the airport at Talkeetna and looked at the various different operations offering a flightseeing of Mt. Denali. K2 Aviation seemed to have the best aircraft and most professional facility. We opted for the air tour which included a landing on a glacier near the mountain itself.

We were issued boots and then greeted by our pilot, Stan. Our aircraft was a vintage de Havilland Otter that had been upgraded with modern avionics and a turbine engine. It appeared to be a very well maintained aircraft. After a short safety briefing, we were in the air, heading for the mountain.

There really is no better way to see Denali up close. Weather plays a big factor in determining how close you can get to the mountain and what you can see, but we got lucky with our trip. The views were truly amazing and I managed to get numerous pictures as our pilot wound his way around the numerous mountain peaks. .

Landing on the glacier was fun and the view of the mountain from that location was the best. One minute the peak was covered with clouds and then it was out in the clear.

Soon we were all loaded up and heading off the glacier. After a little more canyon flightseeing, we were on our way back to the airport.

We saw many interesting and wonderful sights on our 12 day Alaska cruise. Without a doubt, the K2 experience was the highlight of the entire trip.

Review Text:
For a person who always wants the window seat when flying commercially, this is a dream come true! Everyone has a window seat and a view that is beyond imagination. Clouds won't block YOUR view of Denali, because you'll fly above the clouds.
The Summit Tour is at an altitude that makes it important for you to have oxygen, so everything you've ever heard by a flight attendant is put into action. The pilot tells you how to secure your oxygen mask at the right time during your flight. It's totally comfortable.
You do have to step on the scale when you check in at the office of K2, because they wisely balance the plane and give you assigned seats. This was a great time for my husband and me to weigh about the same (even though he's several inches taller than I am!) because there was no question about us getting to sit side-by-side.
We were blessed with a beautiful, sunny day so making our reservation ahead of time worked out well. Taking this tour on a dreary day might not have been as glorious.
Planning your trip so that you're in Talkeetna for a couple of days could allow you to book a spontaneous flight when you have a perfect day for flying. There are plenty of interesting things to do in Talkeetna. My husband especially appreciated it when I spent more time down at the river taking pictures instead of in all of the sweet shops unloading cash.
Going the extra mile and taking the Summit Tour was worth every dollar that it cost.

Review Title: Phenomenal Customer Service created the best lemonade out of lemons
Review Text: We arrived in Talkeetna with a Summit tour with glacier landing booked. Unfortunately, Denali had other plans, weatherwise, so K2 allowed us to push our reservation to the following night in the hopes things would clear.  As that flight got closer, the mountain started to clear but not quickly enough, so they offered us a valley tour instead, so we could at least get up and see Talkeetna, the rivers, and the glacial landforms. This was our last night in Talkeetna area so we decided to take them up on the offer. The others booked for the flight did not, so it wound up being us and the pilot, Bill. We hopped into a Cesna 185 and after an extensive safety review, headed up. Bill said he wanted to fly and asked if we want to explore a bit - see what we might be able to see. we, of course, said yes, he told the office the flight might be a bit longer and off we went.  He took us up to see if Denali might be peeking out above the low clouds, but she wasn't, and so he went through the holes in the clouds to see what was clear. In the end, we made it all the way up the Ruth Glacier, almost to the amphitheater, and saw bears, moose, amazing glacial forms, and so much more. Becuase it was just us and no one else was up there, we were able to circle back when there was something interesting (ice cave, bear, giant ice fissures that have a technical name, ...) and overall just had an amazing personalized tour of the whole. it was far beyond what we expected and truly amazing. Bill was a great pilot - friendly and obviously incredibly competent - we never were nervous on this first small plane experience for both of us - never got sick... it was all in all an unbelievable experience - a memory we will cherish forever.

Review Text:

We wanted to do the summit tour but they had too much cloud cover to do that trip but suggested we do the grand circle tour as they were watching a clearing trend. We had a 6:30 pm flight scheduled and were to check in at 6:00 regarding the weather. The west side of the mountain was still too clouded in for them to want to book the grand circle tour as you would be in the clouds all the while on that side. We were given the option to cancel with a full refund, change to tomorrow in hopes of clearing or take the Denali flyer route which had a perfectly clear view of Mt. McKinley, Mt. Review Text:
Highly recommend doing a flight tour with K2! They were great to work with and have upstanding and fair business practices. How they approached our tours and rearrangement of them said a lot about them and I would absolutely use them again in the future. We booked 2 flight excursions with them for mid-June 2018. One was a sea plane/hiking tour. The other was the Grand Denali tour w/ glacier landing. Unfortunately, the sea plane/hike tour was cancelled because of the long winter and the lake had not yet thawed so they could not land and get to the hiking trail. K2 was excellent in communicating this cancellation to me, explaining why, and refunding our deposit. The Grand Denali tour w/ glacier landing was also modified. The weather around Mt. Denali was not ideal for seeing the mountain, surrounding area, or doing a landing. K2 easily worked with us to reschedule for the next day hoping the weather would get better. When there still was no change in weather, they offered to give us a full refund or book us on a different flight tour which would go south towards Anchorage/Seward and would include seeing glaciers (but no landing). They adjusted the price for this modification. The weather was better south. We opted to do this tour instead and it was fantastic! Seeing glaciers from the air and flying close to huge mountains was incredible. The pilot was extremely experienced and narrated our tour with some great information and pointed out landmarks. On the way back, he managed to catch sight of the very peak of Mt. Denali which had cleared for a few moments and we could see the top!

A few people in our crew felt a little nauseous during the flight. If this happens to you, I recommend removing the headset. You won't be able to hear the pilot, but I found that removing the headset also eliminated the queasy feeling. I think the headsets push against your ears/temples and can cause some people to feel sick.

We love K2 and are looking forward to coming back to Talkeetna again to hopefully get in the Grand Denali Tour w/ glacier landing next time!

Review Text:
My wife and I were excited to schedule our air-tour of Denali with a glacier landing. When we arrived at K2 on the morning of our flight, however, we were told that they could not fly over much of the park due to the weather and suggested that we re-book for that afternoon.

We were not bothered by the rescheduling and found lots to do in Talkeetna to kill the time. When we returned in the afternoon, the sales clerk told us that we could not land on the glacier due to weather conditions, but that we could see the "Matanuska Glacier." Not knowing the area, we agreed to the flight. We were disappointed not be able to do a glacier-landing, but understood that K2 does not control the weather.

Once in the air, however, we learned for the first time that the Matanuska Glacier was not even part of Denali National Park! Instead, we made a heading towards Anchorage. Had we been told that the Matanuska Glacier was not part of DNP, we would have rebooked for another day when we could have seen the park from the air! My biggest disappoint from our three days in Talkeetna and three days outside of DNP was that we never saw that awesome place from the air, and K2 did a poor job explaining to us that we wouldn't be seeing the park from our flight. Having spent a large wad of cash on this flight, we could not afford to book another flight over DNP later in our trip.

Moreover, our view from the plane was bad. Our plane was a dual-engine plane, and we were seated over the engines. We could not see an unobstructed view of the glacier below us and most of our time on the fight was spent look at the engines.

In summary, this was a very expensive excursion and lacked the "bang for the buck."

Review Title: Stunning Views, Wonderful pilot, Smooth Flight
Review Text:
I could not recommend taking a K2 flying tour more. It was the highlight of our trip to Alaska and one of the most unforgettable experiences I've ever had.

K2 watched the weather carefully and made sure we went up at a time when the viewing would be good. We really appreciated their diligence about the weather to ensure a good viewing experience. Given the potentially flexible nature of the flight time, I would recommend planning only activities that can be rescheduled on the same day as your flight tour. We just did a local hike that day, so it was easy to flop our schedules to accommodate the flight time change. We also ended up on a better tour without paying extra since our rescheduled time was to go with others who had booked a longer tour.

The plane itself was comfortable and offered great views from every seat. Our pilot made the experience extra special by sharing information about everything we were seeing as well as happily answering any questions we had. He was also diligent about making sure everyone on both sides of the plane got to enjoy views of the best sights.

The one complaint I would have is that we were confused about being picked up for our flight. When we signed up, the form asked for a pick-up location and gave us a pickup time, but we were actually expected to get there ourselves. Getting there wasn't an issue, but the confusion about what we were supposed to do was frustrating. They also didn't call us when they knew our flight would be rescheduled. They were just going to wait for us to check in at the location to tell us. Luckily, our lodging owner called over there for some other customers and found out that they wouldn't be flying until the afternoon and let us know. We then called and we able to reschedule and clarify the pickup situation. This was frustrating at the time, but the experience was so wonderful, I am not docking them any rating points. I would just suggest that you call before you head there to check on the weather and pickup situation.

Review Title: If you're near Denali, it's a must-do.
Review Text:
We had a great experience with K2 Aviation and our pilot, whose name I unfortunately don't remember.

We did the Denali Experience Tour, their most basic, but hadn't planned to do that one. We chose K2 because they had great TA reviews and because they did glacier landings. We had originally booked the third most expensive trip with a glacier landing. But when we arrived, we were disappointed to learn we could not do the glacier landing because there wasn't enough snow to land. From what the pilot told us, there hasn't been enough snow to land for some time this year. So, I feel like they should have contacted us ahead of time so we could have adjusted to not be looking so forward to the landing experience. At best, it was a bad service move. At worst, it was a tactic to avoid potential cancelations because they probably know that people select their company because of the glacier landings. So, that set a bit of a negative tone for us. Instead, they recommended the basic tour with no landing.

In the end, it worked out well. The tour was awesome. We had great weather. Knowing what we know now, I would recommend the basic tour for $220/person. Overall, I would recommend K2 to anyone and would fly with them again. But, I would strongly suggest they let people know ahead of time when their tours require a change.

For photographers:
I found that my 70-200 mm lens was ideal. The 16-24mm was just too wide and captured parts of the aircraft and my 150-600 was way too cropped in for the aerial landscapes.

Review Text: We took this float plane to hike up in Denali National Park.  I'm terrified of small planes but this was too cool to be afraid of!   The flight was amazing! The hike was not strenuous but the scenery was beautiful and unique.  It was very cool to be 15 nautical miles from the summit of Denali with no one around.  We hiked with a guide from Alaska Alpine Adventures, Andrew who was very knowledgeable.  On our flight back to Fish Lake our pilot (I think his name was Bryan ) flew us up into another valley and circled moose for us to see from both sides of the plane.  Each of our kids got to serve as 'co-pilot' sitting up front and it was a big hit for both kids.  We recommend this tour !

Review Title: Awesome, easiy the best thing we did in the week we were in alaska
Review Text:
We went on the K2 fly and hike adventure, not the land on a glacier flight. We are super glad that we did. The fly and hike starts with a float plane take off from a local lake and about a 30 minute flight up glaciers to backside lake and another glacial lake landing. The flight was incredible, the pilot amazingly smooth and the sights were wow. People talk about going on a helicopter, which is cool, but the float plane is special.

At the lake a guide takes you on a two hour hike around the edges of a glacial lake. This is a glacial moraine and alpine environment so its rocky with great views. We were lucky to have just the four of our family on the hike so the guide took us out a little farther and up a mountain stream. It was amazing.

The hike is a real hike and we were very happy to have worn our hiking boots, pants and brought our poles. Shorts are possible but not preferable. The weather was yucky so we did not see Denali, but it was right there for us to see if it was clearer.

After the hike it was back to base camp for some box wine and snack -- a meat stick and potato chips. Not the best, so if you are picky or want a bigger snack bring some Cliff or Granola bars along. Bring your own water before you get on the plane at the lake side.

The float plane was immaculate, well serviced and the pilot a real pro. On the way back we flew down a different glacier and were able to circle around some local attractions which was really neat.

The best of attractions, safe, unique, cool, amazing, fun, beautiful and an adventure. Really glad we chose this rather than landing on a glacier -- which is something you can also do down in Girdwood.

Thanks K2 for making a really fantastic and lasting memory.

Review Text:
The rule of thumb is that there is a 1 in 3 chance of seeing Denali (Mt. McKinley) without cloud cover. However, on those days that Denali is in the open a flight is a must if your budget can manage it.

One morning following a rainy day we saw that Denali was in view and immediately booked a flight with K2 Aviation, which has a menu of several flight options including landing and walking on a glacier, flying over the lower reaches of the mountain, or flying over and around the entire mountain. We chose the least expensive flight, over the lower reaches of the mountain, because it was the least expensive, my wife is nervous about flying in small planes, and I saw that lenticular clouds were starting to form near the mountain, a sign of high winds and turbulence.

The booking over the phone went fairly quickly; the drive to K2 took about an hour. There was a bit of a wait for processing, and so many people had booked flights that there was little room indoors to sit until departing on our six-passenger Piper Cherokee, which was small but comfortable in terms of seating space and cabin temperature.

We had a capable and well-informed pilot who provided an ongoing narrative that covered the key points of the area and Denali; he also kept a sharp eye out for moose (we spotted several) and bear (no luck). It turned out that high winds cut short the trips of the planes slated to fly above and around the entire mountain, so we were glad we had not opted for that.

We could hear our pilot talking to the control tower from time to time throughout the flight, reporting our location at various key points along the way and keeping track of the numerous other planes in our vicinity (when Denali is visible, all the flight tour services in the area are heavily booked). It is clear that K2's safety protocol is rigorous and well-execute.

Bottom line: A wonderful experience, would do it again, many thanks to K2.

Review Text:
Wir waren schon letztes Jahr hier im Park und konnten den Denali nicht sehen. Dieses Jahr lautete die Wetterprognose günstiger und wir sprachen deshalb am Vorabend im Office von K2 vor. Wir erwarben die letzten zwei Tickets für die «Denali Grand Tour» ohne Gletscherlandung; ein absolutes Highlight wie sich am Folgetag heraus stellte.
Um 10:30 ging es mit einer leistungsstarken DHC-2 Mk III Turbo Beaver los. Unser Pilot Mike, ein Mittfünfziger, begleitete den Flug fundiert, kommentierte von Anbeginn an und beantwortete alle Fragen.
Wir flogen über den Toksitna Glacier ein, kurvten ausgiebig vor Mount Foraker, Mount Hunter und dem Denali und gewannen dabei weiter an Höhe bis auf 12 000 Fuss. Mike steuerte die Maschine so, dass alle Passagiere links und rechts gleichermassen die eindrückliche Gletscherlandschaft geniessen konnten. Auf dem privilegiertem Sitz des Co-Piloten hatte ich dieses Problem allerdings nicht. Wir umrundeten den Denali auf der Westseite, flogen also im Uhrzeigersinn zur Ostseite, von da um den Mount Silverthrone, über den North Fork Glacier zum Sheldon Amphitheater und von da aus über The Great Gorge und den Ruth Glacier nach Talkeetna zurück. Der Flug verlief extrem ruhig und dauerte 1h 30min.
Das Gesehene lässt sich mit Worten nicht beschreiben: Es war unwahrscheinlich schön, ein einzigartiges Erlebnis und für uns wohl einmalig.
Jetzt warte ich gespannt auf das Video, das Standardaufnahmen und zusätzlich 10min. individuellen Film von unserem Flug zeigen soll.

Review Title: Absolutely fantastic ride - worth the price!
Review Text: Having made a reservation to do a flightseeing trip months before we arrived in Talkeetna, I had the very good fortunate to have the sun shining throughout this spectacular trip. My wife opted to not accompany me on this ride. After checking in at K2 Aviation, and then getting weighed, I and others waited a little while for the 4:30 p.m. flight. Finally, the five of us on this trip had our names called and we met our pilot, Craig. We chatted briefly and then walked with him to the airplane. Craig gave us a very thorough review of the plane, the safety features, where things were located, how things worked, etc. Then we climbed in. Since I was the only "single" person on the trip with two other couples, I got to sit in the co-pilot's seat. We put on our head-sets so we could talk with and hear each other during the flight. Craig did his pre-flight checklist, he started the engine, we taxied down the runway, and off we went. Oh, what a ride! Non-stop unbelievable views as we neared then flew into and around Mt. Foraker, Mt. Hunter, Denali itself, the other mountains. We saw gigantic glaciers below us. We saw sheer walls filled with snow pack. We saw mountains above us, below us, in front of us as far as the eye could see. Our pilot shared information about the names of various mountains and glaciers and geologic features. It was absolutely spectacular! Beyond description! After about 1.25 hours, we headed back to the airport. Even as we descended, the gorgeous views of the lakes and rivers below us were breathtaking. All of us marveled at the beauty that we saw during our ride. I took many minutes of videos during the trip which I showed my wife after we deplaned. This plane ride was a major highlight of my (our) trip to Alaska. If you can afford it, do it! It is nothing short of magnificent!

Review Title: Beautiful flight, confused office staff and dishonest pilot took away from what could've been an amazing experience!
Review Text:
Beautiful flight, confused office staff and dishonest pilot took away from what could've been an amazing experience! Doing a land tour on our own prior to a cruise, we decided we would include a sightseeing tour if time and weather permitted. The day we left Denali NP I called K2 Aviation and was told we were doing flights and they would need to have me in the office at minimum 30 minutes prior to flight. We planned a hike in Denali so decided to call after we left Denali and see if there were still seats available. After we were on the road for a bit and I got a cell tower signal I called K2 Aviation. I was told there was seats available to accommodate our family of 4 and I could either book it over the phone or just wait until we arrived. We were still about an hour away so I was a bit concerned that the seats may be sold by the time we got there. I was assured that was unlikely as it was an empty plane and they could do whatever tour we wanted. I was told there were two flights we could choose either 6:30pm or 7:00pm. I told the lady on the phone that it would be after 6pm so we would probably have to take the 7pm flight since she also said we would have to be in the office 30 minutes prior to our flight. Since my cell service was not very good and getting worse I told her we would wait until we got there, as she had suggested, to reserve with our names. We rushed to get there omitting a few stops/pullouts along the way (boo, as Denali was out in plain view).

We get to the office and are inside by 6:20pm only to be told they weren't sure there were enough seats for us and the flight was at 6:30. I told them I was told over the phone that there was another flight at 7pm. The girl said that flight was moved up to 6:30 to accommodate guests who had to be back for a "Princess" tour departure. She said she would ask the dispatcher. As I was waiting another person came up and asked if they could help. I explained the other girl was checking on the flight. Eventually one of them came back and said they could take us on the 6:30 flight. I said that's only in 10 minutes, is there time? She said she would check and then I was told there was actually two flights, but they were both at 6:30. Then another person told me one would leave after the other and that there was indeed one at 7pm, but that all flights actually had to be in the air by 7pm. We wanted the Denali summit with glacier landing since we had been told over the phone they could do any flight we wanted. However, the girl said both flights were the Denali Experience flights. I doubt we would have rushed there skipping pullouts/viewpoints with fabulous views of Denali for that flight, but since we were already there we decided to take that flight. I said I would take the last flight as it would give us more time to fill out paperwork, go to the restroom, and it would not be rushed to get back due to the "Princess" tour people. So while we were waiting we looked around at shirts and my husband asked the girl if the office would be open for us to buy shirts when we got back. She said yes, so we proceeded outside to wait for our flight.

We all were excited and my son especially was excited. He was first in line standing at the gate with my husband while everyone else sat in chairs and waited. When the pilot came through he even made comment to my son and husband that they were ready to go waiting at the gate. As we ventured out to the plane, the pilot went over some standard safety rules, etc. Then he asked if anyone would like to be his "co-pilot". My son raised his hand and another girl (not sure of age probably around 14-17) raised hers. He told the girl to climb in and looked at my son and said we will switch when we land on the glacier that there would actually be two opportunities to "co-pilot". Since we were at the front of the line we moved to the front seats of the plane so others would not have to be climbing around as they entered and were seated. I didn't think much about it, but our seats had to be some of the worst. I was second row and could not get a clear view for a photo without part of the plane in the photograph. It wasn't great, but it was still beautiful The weather was beautiful and the landscape is amazing! We had a great flight and landing on the glacier. Other planes were there and we were the last to leave since we were the last flight. So at one point we were the only plane on the glacier, which was nice. However, as we were getting ready to get back into the plane I overheard the pilot tell a woman to climb on up in the seat beside him. I stopped and turned around and said I thought (I said my son's name) was going to get to co-pilot on the return. The pilot kind of hemmed around and said well, you can't really see from there anyway. I said well, I understood he would get that chance on the way back and he was looking forward to it. The pilot looked at my 13 y/o son (who is small for his age) and said well you can't really see anything from there anyway. He continued to say all of the controls would block his view from the front. I said well he was looking forward to it. The pilot told the lady to go ahead. Needless to say my son was crushed! My son is a bit reserved and doesn't speak up for himself much so he remained quiet, but I could see the look on his face he was obviously disappointed. The pilot had basically told him he could co-pilot on the return, but then gave that opportunity to someone else. The part that made my husband most upset was the fact that the pilot was condescending by saying the control panel would make it harder for him to see! Actually there is a wall between the 1st row and the pilot cockpit area. So the only view from the seat we were in was from the side window anyway! The co-pilot still would have the side window to see out of! So no, Mr. Pilot, that was a lie! The view would not have been worse from the co-pilot seat!

So when we landed he turned around and told my son that after he parked he could climb into the co-pilot seat and see what it was like if he wanted! Seriously?! When the plane came to a stop the lady in the co-pilot seat handed the pilot a tip. I sure hope he got what he deserved from that tip, because he lost the $50 tip from us! There were four of us (also have a 12 y/o daughter) so our plan was to tip $50. When we exited the plane I asked my husband if he was going to stop by the office to get the shirts we picked out. He said "nah, I don't want any". He then looked at my son and asked if he wanted a shirt (we had all picked out shirts), but my son just shook his head no. He was obviously crushed. So we headed straight for the car and left. After we left I reminded my husband I had wanted to purchase the video of our flight, but forgot because I was so upset over what had happened. I honestly don't remember much about the return flight as I was so upset and disappointed for my son that I was distracted.

I want to emphasize that it's not that I expect my son to have had the opportunity over anyone else, but it was the fact that the pilot and told him he could have that opportunity on the return flight and then gave it to someone else. Then the pilot told my son he wouldn't be able see over the controls anyway. Horrible! My daughter is 12 y/o and the only reason she didn't raise her hand to co-pilot was because she knew it meant a lot to her brother and she wanted him to have that opportunity.

So, why two stars? I believe the experience could have been amazing! The planes seem to be good condition, but I can't vouch for sure. I deducted for the miscommunication from the office staff over the phone vs. when we got there. Not to mention that I was getting different info from different people even after I was physically in the office. Finally, the dishonesty of the pilot. I believe a company is only as good as the people who work there. So a confusing office staff and dishonest pilot takes away 3 stars! I wish we had taken our time driving and experienced the beautiful scenery along our drive and skipped this tour. I'd rather have not had the experience than to see my son treated so poorly! With such beautiful landscape, this should have been nothing short of an amazing experience!

Oh, and I want to mention that although we were the last flight and the last to leave the glacier, our pilot had to slow down as he had caught up with the plane that left several minutes before us. Apparently some of the Princess people were also on our plane and he was rushing to get them back! So we landed right behind the other plane.

Now to help those who plan to take this tour anyway here are the tips I'd offer:

Bring: Camera, a jacket (wasn't terribly cold on the glacier), sunglasses, and extra cash for gratuities in the event you have a great experience and wish to tip the pilot.

Make advance reservations and don't rely on the info given over the phone to wait until you get there.

If you have a glacier landing flight they have complimentary glacier boots that fit over your shoes prior to you taking the flight.

Most importantly have no expectations!

Review Title: One of the main goals on our bucket list for this trip!
Review Text:
My husband and I traveled to Alaska mid-April planning to do as much as possible in the "shoulder season" - when winter activities have stopped & summer ones haven't started. Two of the most important goals were to see the northern lights (more on that later) and to do a flightsee trip out of Fairbanks to Denali. Though we weren't able to get a flight reservation made before we left home, our hostess at Meandering Moose Lodge in Fairbanks was quite helpful to get us onto a flight with just a little over an hour's notice! The K2 staff were so friendly, accommodating, and thorough as they took our information and set us up for the flight. (There are several different types of flights available , and K2 will definitely work with you to get you on the flight of your choice.)
The short distance from the Lodge to K2 enabled us to get there quickly, and before we knew it we were boarding the bright red Beaver plane along with 4 others and our pilot, Patrick. The weather couldn't have been more perfect, there was no turbulence the entire trip, and Patrick did an excellent job of constantly informing us about the geography, geology, and history of what we were seeing. All of us wore headphones & microphones, so were able to ask Patrick questions at any point.
This was a fantastic once-in-a-lifetime experience for us, as we were able to see Denali and the other mountains from every direction. Glaciers 3 miles wide, tectonic plate uplifts, two climbers who looked so tiny 1,000 feet below us, rock walls only 300-400 feet away, the top of beautiful Denali - these memories and so many more made our flight with K2 Aviation something we'll always treasure!
Oh, and about those Northern Lights - don't let anyone tell you that mid-April is too late. We saw them one night at Healy, and 4 nights in a row in Fairbanks. Spectacular!

Review Title: The highlight activity of Alaska!!!  My pictures don't do it justice!
Review Text:
There are a few places in the world where pictures just don't work. The Grand Canyon, the Sistine Chapel, the Dancing House of Prague to name a few. What you will see on a glacier landing flight might top any of your lists, it certainly tops mine.

The easiest way to explain just how MASSIVE these mountains and glaciers are can be summed up by a question we asked our pilot. It appeared that he was flying extremely close to the mountains, so we asked him how far away we were from the mountains. He said about 1/2 a mile. The mountains are so huge that our normal perception of distance was off by a magnitude.

Landing on the glacier on the plane skis was phenomenal. Getting outside, walking on some of the world's thickest ice, and realizing how tiny we all are to this expanse of nature was awe-inspiring.

I enjoyed every minute of this adventure.

A hint to those who want the best views...ask to sit in the co-pilots seat. I did on the way back and being able to see out of the cockpit window was spectacular.

Now that I am writing this, my words are barely doing this activity justice. Stop reading! Book it!

Review Text: I am not afraid of flying but I have a fear of heights, which usually means commercial flight is OK but small aircraft flight is white knuckle.  We flew up to Denali in a DeHavilland Beaver that was two years younger than I am but meticulously maintained and flown beautifully.  Admittedly, my knuckles were white for 15 minutes, but the pilot's skill and the overall stability of the trip won me over and I greatly enjoyed my time in the air.  I would definitely do it again.  If you are an aviation buff, you will enjoy the ride in the Beaver.  A ride in the DeHavilland is like a ride on a Harley... not the fastest ride out there but it has a quality that is classic and as memorable as the scenery.  Make sure you take your earphones off for a bit while in flight to hear and feel the deep rumble only a radial piston engine can give you.  The pilot's narration was packed with great information that was interesting and well researched (unlike the mind numbing prattle of most Alaskan tour bus drivers who drone on for hours about their own idiotic reflections on life).  The views were beyond wonderful... transcendent, if you are lucky enough to have a clear day.  You will want to take stills and videos, so clear up your SDS camera card!  One other note, I noticed that the pilot was in constant communication with ground control and the other pilots in the air with us, regularly exchanging positions and headings.  It was a very reassuring, professional vigilance that characterized the whole experience.  Do this!!

Review Text: We flew over Denali the first of September, 2016.  Not a cloud in the royal blue sky, temperature in the 50's and a bit of wind that somewhat limited flight distance; however, the trip turned out to be an experience of a lifetime. I relate the following to show what an outstanding person our pilot Patrick Carter was, as well as the company K2 Aviation was in going above and beyond what is normally expected. While waiting in office area for flight takeoff, a very elderly gentleman with a cane walking extremely slowly and with carefully measured steps walked in alone.  He had great difficulty even stepping up on the scales to weigh in before takeoff.  I silently thought to myself that he would never have the ability to physically climb up the plane steps and certainly not into the plane.  We, along with the other passengers, were waiting to board the steps into the plane when Patrick started talking to the elderly gentleman.  Much to our surprise, the gentleman told us he was a WWII bomber pilot.  After helping him into the plane, Patrick asked him to sit in the seat beside him which he did. All the passengers had headphones and were able to hear him recount some of his WWII experiences as well as all his discussions about airplanes with Patrick. What an experience it was.  Not only were we viewing scenery that is almost beyond description, but we were transported back in time aboard that WWII bomber plane by listening to discussions between the elderly gentleman and Patrick.  When we arrived back to K2, some of the passengers took pictures of Patrick and the WWII pilot in front of the plane. The company even sent out a van to pick up the gentleman and drive him to his hotel.  These pictures will always remind me of our amazing pilot who was so well versed about Denali and the spectacular scenery, as well as the thoughtfulness and kindness exhibited not only by him, but also of this amazing company.  It truly turned out to be an experience of a lifetime.

Review Title: Weather Cancellation? Ask For A Reschedule - TERRIFIC!
Review Text:
My wife and I spent two weeks in Alaska. We booked/visited nearly a dozen tours/events/museums and this was by far our favorite. Read the other positive comments and look at the photos from other reviewers - they are spot on!

We were scheduled for a fly-over Mt. Denali on Aug 25th, the 100th anniversary of the National Park Service. The fog socked in K2 and we were alerted that our noon-time flight had to be cancelled. Later in the afternoon we met a K2 rep in our hotel and found out that weather was very promising for an early morning flight the next day. We took it - it was great! We were lucky but lesson learned -ask for a re-schedule ASAP.

If you are concerned about motion sickness or a bumpy ride, don't be! This take-off and landing was much smoother than the commercial flights we took to and from Alaska. Our plane was an 8-seater Piper Cub (see my photo). Everybody had a window seat. However, if you sit next to the pilot, your view is slightly obstructed by the instrument panel. We were all supplied with noise reduction headphones so the pilot could keep us informed to the viewing highlights. It was also cool to hear the chatter between the pilots and ground control. Apparently not all flights supply headphones. A couple we talked to later said that their flight from Fairbanks to the Arctic Circle was extremely noisy.

If you plan to take photos, go with a wide to medium-angle telephoto lens WITHOUT the UV Haze filter. There is no need for a long lens and not much room for extra equipment on the plane. They supply a large, secure locker for items that you would like to leave on the ground.

This is one Alaskan tour that we would surely do again!

Review Text: We traveled to Talkeetna, Alaska late this summer with the sole mission of completing the glacier landing on Denali.  Our trip last year was foiled by rain every day.  When we arrived, there was not a cloud in sight, so we immediately traveled to K2 Aviation in order to take full advantage of the beautiful weather.  The weather this year completely caught us off-guard for the good.  We hadn't made any advance reservations for this trip, but had planned to accomplish the flight, weather permitting.  What a pleasant surprise.  We were greeted by K2 personnel and the trip was outlined and priced for us and we immediately booked a flight within just a few minutes.  All aspects of the flight were explained and our questions answered thoroughly and completely.  We were soon introduced to our pilot, Patrick.  What a surprise to discover that he was from our home state.  With just a few pre-flight instructions, we were off to the wild blue yonder.  The scenery was absolutely breath-taking.  The glacier landing was smooth and awesome.  Our pilot got so close to the mountain on the flight over that it seemed that you could reach out and touch the mountain.  Patrick took some snap shot of us with the plane on the glacier and after a reasonable amount of time there, we were once again airborne to the vastness of the Denali range.  Upon return to K2, we learned that our flight had been recorded and we immediately ordered a copy.   The K2 video staff advised us that if we had any photos taken while on the glacier, to email them and they would incorporate them into the video for us to further personalize our project.  The hard part was limiting the number of photos.  When the USB video arrived, we have nearly worn it out showing it to family and friends.  What a treat to have them experience what we saw on our trip.  Thank you to the folks at K2 for a wonderful experience.  We are already planning a return trip with kids and grandkids and look forward to flying with K2 again.  The HD video is as close to the real thing as you can get.  I HIGHLY recommend this when you fly with K2.  Most folks don't realize that Denali is only viewable to visitors about 30% of the time.  And we can certainly attest to that from our trip there last year.  But to our good fortune, we saw it cloud-free for six consecutive days....something that even the locals were amazed to see. The K2 flight experience was something that I will cherish for many years to come.  And the flight video allows us to relive this near-miraculous feat over and over again.

Review Title: Great Company Offering an Unforgettable Experience!
Review Text:
This is one of the finest flightseeing Air Taxi operations I've ever flown on, and I've flown on quite a few. Incredibly friendly staff, superb pilots, and some of the best airplane maintenance I've seen (I work in Aviation). The planes are routinely painted, the ramp and main office are clean and well-maintained, and the service from start-to-finish is absolutely top-notch. Prices are reasonable for what you're getting (and you have to realize that they have to pay for their planes, fuel, maintenance, insurance, payroll, glacier landing permits, etc., plus make a profit). And once you are in the air and you see Denali ("Mt. McKinley") starting you in the face as you look out your window, you will forget how much you paid, quite frankly. There is NOTHING like landing on a glacier in the shadow of Denali on a clear day! They even offer "loaner" sunglasses for your flight if you don't have any of your own (and you WILL need them--the glare of light off the snow in the mountains will overwhelm your eyes)!

Zero complaints, I can't recommend this company enough! Make sure you bring your camera and a decent jacket, it gets cold on the glaciers and you won't want to miss photographing the spectacular views that await you!

Review Title: The Clouds Tried To Hide Denali
Review Text:
Our original flight around Denali and a glacier landing was not possible due to the weather conditions (they had only been able to fly minimally the previous two weeks), but K2 offered us an alternate flight that would still allow us to see the lower mountains and the glaciers. Somewhat disappointed we decided to take the alternate flight.

The rugged peaks of the lower mountains and the huge glaciers were breathtaking even on this cloudy day. We were not disappointed that we had taken the alternate flight.

Our pilot monitored the radio and listened to where other pilots in the area were able to see through the clouds and determined that if we climbed we may see Denali peeking through. So up he went and on his final circle upwards we saw it, the peak of Denali briefly poked out of the clouds to reveal its beauty. We wanted to see all of Denali in all her grandeur, however, being able to see the peak on a day where we did not expect to see her at all, made our day.

K2, despite the weather, was able to make our trip to Talkeetna and the Denali area worth the trip. The company was professional and gave us a great experience while keeping us safe.

Review Title: A Highlight of Our Trip - K2 Was Great
Review Text:
Our flight-seeing trip was a great experience. After day after day of heavy overcast and rain during our week in Alaska, the day of our scheduled 4 hour Fly-Hike looked promising.

Arriving at K2, they were very up-front about the fact that the weather for the afternoon in the mountains was expected to change dramatically - they were confident about getting us in, but might not be able to get us out! They checked with several pilots and the weather reports and offered us 3 possibilities: cancel with a refund, go for it and possibly spend the night camped at the destination (they're prepared for that) or switch to a flight-only trip. We chose the flight-only option (1-1/4 hrs) and wound up as the only passengers on a 6-seater plane piloted by Daniel.

What a tremendous outing! Daniel was enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and skillful. We headed up over the clouds, over several glaciers, over fields and rivers viewing the landscape from multiple angles and altitudes. The photo opportunities never seemed to end and the knowledge we gained inestimable.

I can't say enough about how well we were treated - honest and forthright. I've dealt with other tourist oriented companies that would do anything to hold on to their fees, but K2 did the right thing right out of the gate.

Thank you Daniel and K2 for a perfect end to our trip.

PK
