Review Title: Awesome isn't big enough to describe it!
Review Text:
We booked the Grand Denali tour, but due to weather we could only do the Denali Flyer due to weather. (We were charged appropriately.) As a private pilot myself, I fully appreciated why the change was made. The ticketing staff was open, informative and prompt. We did get an email after we made our reservation that said another confirmation would be coming...which never arrived. I called them a few days beforehand to confirm and everything was fine.

You get goretex over boots before your flight. Excellent equipment. Our aircraft was a DeHavilland Otter equipped with wheels and skis. Turbine driven, seats 10 plus the pilot. One passenger gets to sit in the right hand seat up front. Everyone has a window with a good view, easy access and lots of leg room. Head sets provided were excellent quality and connected to the intercom so we could hear the radio traffic and could converse with the pilot.

There are simply no words that fully capture and convey the size of not only Denali, but the entire Alaskan Range. There is a reason over 700 photos have been posted to the K2 Aviation Trip Advisor page.

The pilot was 100% professional (Thanks Chris!) and gave a great description of each of the landmarks and maneuvered to move us away from turbulence smoothly and quickly. The glacier landing was the highlight of our trip. While on the ice we got to witness an avalanche that occurred way up the mountain. (Which I uploaded a picture with an arrow pointing it out.)

Their site says to bring sunglasses, jacket and a camera. I'd suggest a second camera and spare batteries because you will be taking pictures non stop.

Once again, there is no way to fully capture the size and scale of Alaska in words. You can only experience it, and K2 delivers big time.

(I bought one of their ball caps made from oilskin. Heavy Duty and excellent quality also!)

Review Text:
My family and I toured with K2 on a day that didn't have great weather. We were supposed to have a flightseeing tour and glacier landing at 1 pm, but because the weather was poor, the company worked with us to make sure we could still try to get up in the air later that day. The company, to my surprise, was adamant that we would not just eat the money if we could not do the flightseeing due to bad weather; instead, we would be reimbursed. But fortunately we were able to reschedule for 5 pm that day, and the weather had cleared somewhat by then. We couldn't do the glacier landing part, only the flightseeing part, but the company again stated that we would be reimbursed the difference. We were extremely grateful for this policy of theirs.

The tour itself was fabulous and truly the best experience of ours in Alaska. It was about an hour and a half, with us getting excellent views of Denali and especially Foraker. We were wowed by the experience. The entire reason my mother wanted to come to Alaska was to see the mountains, and boy did we see them. I cannot imagine coming to Alaska without seeing the mountains from the sky.

Our pilot, Chris, was sure to explain to us which mountains were which, and did a great job at giving us information about what we were seeing while also giving us time to absorb the sublimity of it all. We certainly felt we were in capable hands up in the skies.

Review Text:
Pre-booked on our Princess Cruisetour, we went for the Denali summit flightseeing tour with K2 Aviation, located at the airport in Talkeetna. A shuttle bus goes from the Princess Lodge to Talkeetna on the hour, and from Talkeetna to the lodge on the ½ hour. We took the shuttle to K2, where we checked in and then were weighed (for weight distribution in the plane), with all clothes, camera, etc. you were taking with you. The plane was a Piper Navajo Chieftain with an unpressurized cabin. Our group had 8 passengers. The pilot gave us an extensive safety talk, including testing the oxygen masks we’d be using over 12,000 ft., and what to do in case we get stranded—an unlikely but real possibility up the mountain.

We took off from Talkeetna, across the flats, between there & the mountain. As we neared the mountain, the view got more and more awesome by the minute. We also had on a headset and microphone so that we could talk and hear the driver and each other (very noisy propeller engines), and a snug seatbelt. The plane is equipped with big nice windows for viewing and picture taking. Everyone has a great view. While circling the mountain, the pilot said that we were within ½ mile of the rock faces and summit. It felt like you could reach your hand out and touch it. It was breathtaking, fantastic, and beyond words to describe. We were able to see several very long glaciers, the summit of the mountain, and the surrounding mountains. From the distance, you have no idea how much detail—valleys, crags, rock, etc. nor how immense and vast the mountain is. There is an unimaginable amount of ice, snow and rock up there. We were able to see where the base camps are for the mountain climbers. I took dozens of pictures trying to take it all in.

K2 also has flights that land on a glacier, but do not go to the summit. The passengers are outfitted with appropriate gear. Those planes fly at a much lower altitude.

I had some trouble with the altitude, but the others in the group did fine. The pilot and other people at K2 very diligently made sure I was OK before letting us leave for the shuttle back to the hotel. If you have heart or respiratory issues, you may want to check with your doc before doing this tour, just in case. All in all this was an amazing experience, and I would do it again if I had the chance.

He greeted all of us with the same professional yet friendly manner as the other staff. He took us through a safety briefing and then helped us get seated AND everyone got a headset with the ability to talk back and forth with the pilot! I have participated in several "ride" flights and, in my experience, K2 makes certain to slow down the process and let you enjoy the moment vs rushing you in and out treating you more like a number. K2 opened my eyes to a breathtaking part of the US that I wish everyone could see first hand. With that being said, if you have a chance to get the video from your flight, do it!!! Review Text:
Taking a K2 flight to see the Denali area from the air may be expensive, but it is worth it. While what you can see is weather dependent, the pilots will do their best to make sure you see as much as possible. They are in constant contact with each other by radio, sharing the current visibility of various features to help each other provide the best views for the passengers. We saw only a few glimpses of Denali itself, but the other sights, especially the glaciers, were excellent, making the flight worthwhile.

A few tips: First, if you are interested in a glacier landing, be advised that this is never a sure thing and it depends on the weather and how firm the ice in the landing areas on the glaciers is on any given day. The day we went, some glacier landings were cancelled (they refund a portion of the fare when that happens), and a few were able to be completed.

There is an advantage to a glacier landing that has nothing to do with glaciers. The planes that are equipped for glacier landings (skis on the landing gear) have wings above the passenger area of the plane, making for unobstructed views down toward the ground. Planes that are not scheduled for glacier landings have wings below the passenger area of the plane, which partially obstructs the view looking down. So if you can afford it, you'll get a better view if you choose a glacier landing flight.

Another tip: We chose a non-glacier landing, and the box beam supporting the wings passes through the passenger compartment right near the place where you'd put your feet, for one of the rows of seats, so if you can, avoid that row. Also avoid riding with the pilot in the front; although that sounds cool, you don't see as well from there due to the instrument panel. Surprisingly, the back seats in the plane might actually be the best for this type of plane.

Our flight was nominally an hour long, but we were in the air for about 90 minutes. I think this was just a reflection of K2's desire to please customers, and not due to any flight restrictions. Plan your day accordingly, for the flight to take longer than you might expect.

Review Text:
My fiance and I spent two days hiking the Kesugi Ridge, staring at Mt. McKinley and decided once we got off the trail, we wanted to see McKinley up close and personal. We're pretty frugal so it took a lot of debate on whether or not to invest in the flightseeing tour. At 6 pm in the evening, we finally decided IF we could still get on a flight that evening, we would take the financial plunge and do it.

The first person I talked to on the phone at K2 was helpful, he explained what routes they were flying, the cost, etc. After hanging up and going over the information I learned with my fiance, I then called back to clarify a few things. The next person I spoke with, I believe her name was Stephanie, was not as friendly. When I questioned how she came up with the total price, she sounded put out and stated there were taxes and "other" fees. I wanted to know what the other fees were so pressed her a bit more and she finally said national park fees. Since we had been in Denali Park a few days ago, we had already paid these. Had I not pressed her, I wonder if we would have paid them twice. Aside from that interaction, everything else about the tour was wonderful.

We went on the blue route with a glacier landing. Our pilot was extremely informative and made sure both sides of the plane had great views of the various peaks, base camp areas, etc. We had plenty of time to spend on the glacier and luckily for us, had a nice, clear day. There are so many amazing things you see from the plane that you would never get to experience on foot, that even this frugal person (we tent camped most of our 10 day trip) highly suggests shelling out the bucks for this excursion.

Review Title: A once in a lifetime opportunity
Review Text:
A once in a lifetime experience and a MUST while touring in Alaska. This was the first activity during our 10-day Alaskan experience I booked (based on reviews from others), and it was also the activity I looked most forward to on our trip. K2 Aviation exceed my expectations in every way possible! I surprised my husband with this activity and he too, not only had a great experience but couldn't stop talking about (and neither of us can a month later)!

We originally booked the Denali Grand Tour (the package that flies around the North side of Denali) but due to weather were downgraded to the McKinley Flier. K2 Aviation was very accommodating and communicative, providing us with a refund between the two packages (in a very speedy time frame). Even with the downgraded package, we had an amazing time and still had an amazing experience in Denali National Park. It's something neither of us will ever forget!

In addition to the flight, we added in the glacial landing. While the views are out of this world, the glacial landing was unbelievable! Definitely bring a camera and sunglasses along, but if you do a glacial landing, lift up your sunglasses for a few seconds. I hail from a land of snow six months of the year and have never seen such a bright white, and it's something I will never forget.

In addition to our experience, and why we had such a great time, we had an amazing pilot at the helm. Our pilot, Patrick was absolutely amazing and very knowledgeable. He ensured all of us along for the ride had a great time and experience. Patrick is also an avid photographer and was more than happy to take amazing photos of everyone.

If you are traveling to Alaska, what are you waiting for? Book a trip (and add a glacial landing) through K2 Aviation NOW!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
The people booking the flights were rude. We were on standby for flights and waited. After an hours wait we asked for a status update and were told that the next possible flight was an hour and a half away. While we were waiting, a gentleman asked if he could wait to go up alone. Instead of giving him options regarding costs for a private flight, they very rudely told him that he had paid for a seat not a plane.

We found a company that would take our phone number for standby, walked around town for awhile, and finally went up. My advice; find a less corporate outfit to experience the mountain!

Review Text: My wife and I did a flight with K2 kind of on a whim.  We had planned to do lots of hiking in Denali, and along the Kesugi ridge in Denali State Park.  But 2 weeks before our visit I broke my leg -- so the hiking option was gone.  The morning we arrived in Talkeetna, the weather was nice, so we decided to try a sightseeing flight.  We did the short "McKinley Experience" flight, because I was concerned about the cost (and I am a pilot, so I've seen lots of mountains from the air).  The only option available for us on short notice that day was one with the glacier landing.  That turned out to be the BEST part of the entire flightseeing experience -- even though I probably would not otherwise had paid the extra cost.  In hindsight, we are really glad we did the glacier landing because it turned what would have been a nice tour into a great experience.  Even though I have a couple thousand hours of flight time as a pilot, the glacier landing and takeoff were a unique experience and well worth the expense.  So my personal advice would be that if you are trying to decide between a longer, more expensive flight -- or a shorter flight with a glacier landing, definitely choose the glacier landing!

Review Text: We want to express our appreciation to Chip Sonn, our K2 pilot for our fantastic late afternoon/evening flight excursion while recently visiting Talkeetna, Alaska.  As part of our planned Land/Cruise tour, we did not want to miss this opportunity – and glad that we took the extra effort to reschedule through the cruise planning offices to get all 5 of us to be able to attend as a family together on this flight.  We flew across a varied array of physiographic regions in and around Denali Park while Chip extolled about a combination of historical/geological/topographical/mountain climbing/gold mining aspects related to this diverse region of Alaska.  Climbing in altitude up through the sinuous glacial flows between spired peaks for repeated glimpses of the great mountain – Denali was truly awe inspiring.  How many pictures is enough?  However, in all honesty, landing on the glacier with our wonderful pilot was truly the greatest event to remember as a family from our land/cruise tour from all of Alaska.  Standing together as a family in the quiet Pika Glacier valley with great spires around us and peacefully reflecting on family and life was truly one of those “Picture Perfect Moments” that we will treasure forever.  We all agreed during our ride back to the hotel, that this adventure would likely become our best family activity together for the entire 12 days of land and sea excursions – and now having completed our trip and returned home, we can confirm that this flight and landing on the glacier was indeed our best activity as a family together in Alaska.  The K2 planes are safely maintained and their staff and pilots are the greatest.  We had great peace of mind and felt very secure flying with Chip and the K2 family.  Thanks again for Chip’s time and talent for the great evening of flight together – one we will not forget!

Review Text:
If you had one day in Alaska and had to pick one thing to do, flying with K2 Aviation to Denali National Park for a 3 hour hike (guided by Alaska Alpine Adventures) surrounded by glaciers would fit the bill very nicely.

Upon early arrival at the K2 Aviation office we were greeted with smiles, filled out a simple form, "weighed in", and relaxed on their sunny deck. The facility and grounds were very nice; clean and well kept. A short time later we boarded a van that took us to the float plane dock a few miles away. The driver was pleasant and made sure we were comfortable. Once there we took a few pictures of the surrounding beauty while passengers deplaned and the aircraft was being topped off with fuel. Our pilot Jeff then introduced himself to us, gave us an easy to understand pre-flight safety briefing and made us feel very safe and welcome.

We boarded the aircraft and were airborne in short order. Lift off from the water was imperceptible. I know many factors can contribute to the way an airplane performs in flight, weather, aircraft design, pilot's skills, etc. The de Havilland Beaver was solid and smooth flying. What a great comfortable ride from a great Alaskan bush plane classic. The views were nothing short of phenomenal. This is what those Alaskan nature shows dream of capturing on film. Nothing beats the experience of seeing Alaska from the air with your own two eyes. Our richly experienced and confident pilot kept us engaged by pointing out interesting geography and landmarks. The views of colossal glaciers and majestic Denali (Mt. McKinley) were magnificently surreal. Take plenty of memory for your digital cameras.

We landed on Moraine Lake and touchdown was equally imperceptible. Our hiking guide Elliot greeted us, stored our day bag and gave us trekking poles to begin our three hour hike. He even stuffed our water bottles and our sweaters into his back pack so that our hands could be free to enjoy the hike and take pictures. Elliott was very knowledgeable about the terrain and surrounding beauty of the mountains. It's great to be educated while having fun. His pace matched our abilities and desires. Elliot delivered an enthusiastic and fun adventure.

Upon return to base camp, Elliot set out some chairs for my wife and I and we relaxing at water's edge while he catered crackers, cheese, smoked salmon, and red wine! We had pleasant conversations amid one of the most beautiful and secluded sub-arctic locations known to mankind. We were a bit saddened to leave so soon as the sound of Jeff's plane returned to fly us back to Talkeetna. The flight back was just as breathtaking. Once again we saw incredible glacier features, moose, and a some of the same sights as before but from a different angle...equally impressive.

A huge thanks to all involved in making our tour, safe, enjoyable, and the unforgettable highlight of our summer!

AK residents: get out and enjoy our state with K2 Aviation, (ask for pilot Jeff), and Alaska Alpine Adventures...don't let the tourists have all the fun!

Review Text:
Talkeetna airfield is situated on the right hand side of the road, just before you enter town. As there is only one way into town, you have to pass it. It is a base for a number of operators offering flight sightseeing tours of Mt McKinley and the area. All the operators offer similar packages and prices for the various trips.

We chose K2 Aviation, having flown with Rusts Flying Services in Anchorage on a bear watching trip. K2 is a sister company to Rusts.

In high season it is probably best to book in advance to avoid disappointment. Though this has to be weighed up with the possibility of the weather not being too good.

We arrived at about 4PM on a Sunday and booked for a 7PM departure that evening. We opted for the 90 minute flight and glacier landing. We were not disappointed.

One of the attractions of K2 and some of the other operators are in the type of aircraft they use on the flights. A good number are on De Havilland DHc2 Beavers and DHc3 Otters. Some of these aircraft are around 50 years old and the type is still very common for bush flying in Alaska. This bit of aviation history often goes unnoticed by passengers and is something that should be a selling point. The operators don’t seem to make a big thing of it. (Or maybe passengers will be put off by the age?)

Our flight was on a six seater DHc2 Beaver N121KT, built in 1958. One passenger usually gets to sit up at the front with the pilot. A good safety demo was given prior to boarding. It was also pointed out to us that the aircraft carried overnight supplies etc, in the extreme case the weather turned and we couldn’t return!

The flight was excellent. Real close up views of the glacier, mountains etc. Stunning scenery. All passengers get a window seat. On the Beaver, the rear seats are better than the middle as you don’t have a wing strut in front of you. The view from the middle is still excellent, but photos may get the odd strut in them. After landing you are allowed off the aircraft, as long as you keep nearby. The peace and tranquillity is only shattered for a moment when another aircraft lands or takes off. The evening we went it was a clear blue sky – perfect We had around 25 mins on the snow, watching a couple of other flights land and take off (tip – don’t stand downwind of one when it takes off, unless you want to experience a blizzard!)

The return flight is quicker and comes straight back to the airfield, as most of the sightseeing is done on the way up.

If you get the right weather, this trip will be one of the highlights, if not the highlight of your stay.

Review Text:
We booked this excursion through our Princess Cruisetour, and it was excellent. We were fortunate to have a beautiful, sunny day, and the scenery was just spectacular. Our pilot, Michael, was very understanding and patient while we stored our backpacks. We were initially told by the clerk to hang onto them until we were called, but in reality they should be stored away before your pilot calls you. Good to know for next time, because I definitely want to come back and do the summit tour in the future.

We flew on a DeHavilland Otter, a fixed-wing plane which has skis to land on Pika glacier! These pilots are just amazing how they can land on this glacier. The glacier scenery was beautiful and Michael took an awesome picture of my family (with my iPhone!) in front of the Otter, which later became our Christmas card. My son is interested in becoming a pilot, so he let him sit in the cockpit--the best seat--on the flight back to K2. We had gorgeous views of Denali from the plane--a truly wonderful experience.

There was actually a tent set up further away on this glacier--it amazed me to think people actually set up camp here. This is also the place where mountain climbers start their trek up Denali, (although climbing season had ended when we were there) and it was very sobering to realize how unrealistic that would be for me!

K2 Aviation was great, our pilot Michael was wonderful (and a darn good photographer!), and we were fortunate to fly with them again on our next day's excursion. The Summit Flight is now on my bucket list.

Review Text:
I booked the Denali Grand Tour with glacier landing 5 months before our September trip. I booked it for the afternoon we arrived in Talkeetna so that we had 2 back-up days in case the weather prevented us from going. This was a good move as our first day was solid clouds and rain. We rescheduled for the next day and the weather cleared up enough for us to go, but not enough to do the tour we wanted or to do a landing. The tour we took was less expensive than what we booked so we were only charged for the difference. However, it seemed that everyone was charged a different rate, and walk-ins got the best rate. We paid more because we booked in advance. When we asked them about it we were told pretty much that this is the way it is. It did not leave me with a positive feeling.

The ride itself was full of beautiful scenery. We were there when the leaves were turning so the landscape was full of bright yellows and the dark green of the pine trees. Our plane looked brand new and to be full of the latest technology. We had the seats by the wing supports, so we could only get a clear view front and back, not straight out. I was on the right side. It seemed that all the scenery being described, and our main approach to Mt. McKinley was on the left. The pilot's voice was a little monotone so I stopped listening after awhile since he was mainly describing views to the left. The plane eventually turned so the right could see, but the narration was minimal so I really didn't know what I was looking at. I'm sure I saw Mt. McKinley, but I had no idea at all which peak it was.

All in all, I would recommend taking one of these tours as the scenery is really spectacular, but if I go again I will book with someone else.

Review Text:
CHEAPER IF BOOKED DIRECTLY, but if there are scheduling problems with your cruise line and you're late, it's better to have booked thru the cruise line. There is an option especially to book tours the day you disembark the ship.
The Princess hotel is 50 MILES from Talkeetna. We got off the ship, took a 4.5 hour train to Talkeetna, did a glacier landing flight, then a one hour bus ride to the McKinley Lodge. We were glad we took a flight the same day while in Talkeetna. We had to spend an hour on a bus the next day (each direction) to take our second flight to circle McKinley.
Book early for the time you want. Our train was to arrive at 12:15, but arrived about an hour late, so I was glad our flight wasn't until 3 pm. (This is also why I'm glad I booked thru Princess. The cost was higher, but we didn't have to worry about the time because it was the cruise line's fault if we were late.) The clouds cleared just in time for our glacier landing, too. If we'd booked earlier, we wouldn't have been able to land. I checked online before we left home and by then, then next available tours were after 6 pm, so I was glad I booked ahead. You may not want to spend five hours in Talkeetna unless you had another tour planned. It's a small town and there isn't that much to see or do unless you're hiking or taking a tour. You won't spend hours shopping like you would in a larger town. Most Alaskan stores have pretty much the same things, anyway.

Some staff is not that knowledgeable and pilots are (understandably) seasonal- I caught ours lowering the visor for tips on landing the plane at the end of one of our flights.
The pilots give commentary, but also have to stay in constant contact with the ground and each other for safety reasons. There are a few planes in the air and you want your pilot concentrating on safety, not on some bratty kid kicking his seat or irritating passengers who don't shut up.

We took two flights- Glacier Landing and the flight around McKinley summit.
Honestly, the glacier landing was much more interesting. Two planes landed within minutes of each other and we were the first landings in five days, so you may not get to land if it's too cloudy. They said it isn't safe to take off again if it's cloudy above. The pilots are in constant radio contact, though, so they know the location of each plane to prevent accidents. We spent our time looking at the glaciers, mountains, etc. The glaciers have amazing turquoise pools of water and the landscape is a myriad of colors you wouldn't believe. When on the glacier, you can hear a river of water rushing beneath. It was amazing.

The flight around McKinley the next day was novel, but somewhat boring after seeing the glaciers and colorful landscape the day before. You go out to the mountain, circle around and around, then back to the airport. My husband's window fogged, so he didn't see much of anything. (Two rows behind the pilot.) The pilot repeatedly tilts the plane in each direction so both sides can see. My husband was very disappointed in his flight and took only a couple of pictures because he couldn't see anything His pictures were out the window on the OTHER side of the plane and that passenger had her oxygen tubing over the window. For the cost, I feel badly for him, but my flight was good, just a little boring after the first few minutes at the summit.
Take the Glacier Landing Tour. You won't be disappointed even if you don't land. There is a price adjustment or longer flight if you can't land.
I loved our pilot- Rich:)

Review Title: Thanks to K2 for another wonderful, world class mountain flight
Review Text:
Thanks to K2 for another wonderful, world class mountain flight. Ever since we flew with K2 on our climb of Denali, we have been impressed with their friendliness, efficiency, can do attitude, safe operations, experienced pilots and the love of flight and nature they exude.
Without their help we could not have summited Denali back in 1998 as they were able to get a team member in at crucial time. Two years ago we flew with K2 again and the pilot was knowledgeable, the flight was beautiful, the ground staff exceptional.
We flew again last week on a perfect day, in a beautiful and powerful Beaver on skis. Suzzane, the owner of K2 Aviation and the K2 staff, as usual were awesome, flexible and helpful- a great team. Chris our pilot- is a world class aviator. He was also very well informed and shared the local history, flora , fauna, geology and geography with us.
We flew close by by towering cliffs, icefalls, around, above and below jagged peaks. We landed on Denali's Pika glacier and we all jumped out smiling and laughing, overcome by the raw and rare beauty. We walked around on fresh snow on the glacier, surrounded by sun sparkled peaks, with Denali rising above them all. In this grand amphitheater of multi- colored rock and white ice, dark peak and blue sky, the sturdy but nimble looking K2 aircraft was like a small red jewel sitting there on its skis. The kids had snow ball fights, made snow angels and chased each other,laughing and filled with delight. We finished with a family race back to the plane-with Chris our pilot as the finish line.
This summer we have climbed many mountains, competed in rodeos, surfed, skied, skydived, raced, biked, canyoneered and may other things but the flight and landing on the ice was to me the most amazing and awe inspiring experience. Thank you K2 for that flight and for who you are- wonderful, adventurous, kind, expert, and fun to fly with. We love you! God bless you, Dave Eubank, family and all the Free Burma Rangers

Review Title: Diappointed!  Don't book if you have a schedule to keep.
Review Text:
Disappointed!

K2 Aviation has the fancy sign, a prime spot in town, sweatshirts in the front of their office and even coffee, but they lack professional customer service. Alaska has a unpredictable weather pattern and Talkeetna follows the same rules. There are many travelers that come through looking for a flight experience to see Denali or Mt. McKinley. Some on ships that only permit a day to experience. K2 doesn't seem to care. Their daily order of business is to look at the flight weather and then when people check in for the flight, schedule them on the next flight available. They do not tell you to call the morning of or night before. They simply reschedule first come first serve. Therefore if your flight is at 10 and you are asked to reschedule, you might not get a flight until the next day when you go through the same order of events. K2 also is very expensive for what you get. Maybe it is to cover the coffee or the design of their shirts. K2 also only has VFR or visual flight rules. Meaning their pilots can only operate if the clouds are clear or good visibility. This causes for many delays and rescheduled plans.

IFR however has extensively more training and can operate by instruments or instrumental flight rules. IFR certification simply means much less cancelations. After our flight was canceled and we were "rescheduled" to another day much less convieient , we found McKinley Flight Tours, or Fly Denali. http://www.talkeetnaaero.com/about.htm

They were less expensive and we were able to have a reduced price lower than advertised as we were flying last minute. No fancy shirts and their location was less prime, but I would recommend to anyone trying to take a tour. Their company also has IFR pilots. We were so happy with our choice.
Don't waste your time with K2 especially if you are on a cruise.

Review Title: Amazing ending to a incredible trip
Review Text:
Our stay in Talkeetna was the end of an incredible trip and the flight and glacier landing on Denali was an amazing way to end it.
We flew with K2 in June 2013.
We contacted them via email in Jan/Feb 2012 to reserve the flight. All communication was quick and easy.
The day of our flight was cloudy, misty and pretty socked in. Our flight was scheduled for 9 AM, there was no way we were going anywhere so we were asked to come back around noon and check in. At noon we moved back to 2:30. The ladies in the front office area were very helpful with weather updates and scheduling during this time. They were friendly and very easy to work with.
Thankfully at 2:30 there was enough of a break to get some flights in. The cloudy weather had actually helped. It had been so sunny and warm the previous couple weeks that they had not been doing many landing.
If you are hedging on whether to do the glacier landing or not. DO it!! You may never be there again, the cost is well worth the experience. It was amazing, especially when you think only a few actually get to see the mountain, and fewer yet get to stand on it.

The only slightly negative experience of the day was the area to get the over boots and groups together to get out to the planes. A tall gentleman with a pony tail was trying to heard all the humans in some resemblance of groups to get them to the correct pilots. I thought his attitude and approach with getting some of the other flyer's booted up and to the pilots was rude. May have been a long and hectic day but this area could be improved on.
Tony our pilot was not very talkative but is a very skilled pilot. I thoroughly enjoyed flying with him. The flight around the mountain, the landing on and views from the glacier were just spectacular.

With the ease of setting up the flights and the way the office staff helped get us on a flight I would fly with K2 again anytime. They are a safe company that has well maintained planes and exceptional pilots.

Our pilot, Chris, wasn't the most talkative, but most of us just gaped out the window as the majestic Denali kept looming larger in our windows. When we had questions, Chris was knowledgeable in his responses and has been flying with K2 for about 10 years.

The closer we came to the mountains, the more unbelievable the views were. I took many pictures, but none of them do justice to how incredible the actual views were.

We were fortunate that for most of the trip, the mountain was in mostly full view, but by the end of the tour, it was about 50% shouded in clouds. Regardless, every banked turn showed other incredible vistas.

I asked for, and was granted the opportunity, to sit in the co-pilot's seat so I was able to look out both the front and side windows. Be sure to find your pilot and ask early because it's first to ask that is granted that privilege.

Take advantage of the waterproof shoes. You'll need them for a glacier landing. Also, unless it's a particularly cold day, you don't have to bundle up too warmly for the glacier landing. I just had on a long sleeved shirt and was comfortable. But ... if you're cold natured, definitely bring a jacket.

Awesome excursion.

Also, be sure to check for coupons in the Northern Lights Coupon Book. You can purchase them at any Barnes and Noble in AK and for $55 you will save much more than that on most adventures.

Review Title: Flying around Denali is a pilot's dream
Review Text:
I cannot recommend the K2 experience enough. Both the flying and the views were far beyond my expectations. I am a pilot myself and I have read about bush flying for years which gives me a great appreciation of the difficulty and the skill needed to do what K2's pilots do everyday with charm and grace. Their airplanes are in beautiful condition and several are bush plane "classics" including my favorite, the DeHavilland Beaver which they have on skis and on floats.

I was lucky enough to be able to experience several flights with the K2 team and each was a uniquely wonderful experience. My favorite was the flight around the mountains with the glacier landing in the Beaver but the most spectacular views were from the summit flight in the Navaho twin.

My first flight was on a sunny, clear day so I chose the "McKinley Flyer with Landing" in the Beaver on skis. After flying over rivers and glaciers and through passes with incredible views our pilot landed smoothly on a glacier at a spot called "Mountain House". This landing spot has spectacular views of Mount McKinley and surrounding peaks. Standing on the glacier gives you a true appreciation of the immensity of the steep cliffs and granite walls. It was overwhelming! K2 also does this flight in the larger DeHavilland Otter which is also on skis and has windows at each seat. An Otter landed near us while I was on the glacier and one of my favorite photos is of this bright red plane against the clean white snow and blue skies of Mountain House.

The weather is very changeable in the mountains, going from low clouds and overcast to open sunny skies and back within a few hours so some flights will see more than others. My second flight was on a day with low clouds so I opted for a Summit flight in the Navaho. The Navaho has oxygen which allows the pilot to fly above the overcast to the same 20,300 ft. altitude as the top of McKinley. On my flight, the peak was poking up above the overcast into sunny skies and we were able to circle the peak several times at varying altitudes. We were close enough to see the climbing routes and high camps. It was amazing and my photos turned out beautifully! On our return the clouds broke up enough to allow the pilot to descend among the peaks and gorges at lower altitudes so we were able to see the Ruth glacier and Mount Hunter before we returned to the airport.

Whether you are a pilot or not, flying with K2 is a wonderful way to see the Alaska range. It is an experience I will never forget!

Review Title: Pick your flight carefully if you want to do video or photography
Review Text: While I have nothing but really good things to say about the company in general, the plane they chose for our flight left much to be desired as one of my main goals was to take pictures and video. I have never taken a small plane sightseeing flight before, I didn’t realize how critical positioning was if you wish to take photos and video. We flew in a small deHavilland single-engine propeller plane. There were five basic seats for passengers. The only seat that appeared to have good visual access for photography was the front seat on the right next to the pilot. Someone quickly decided he needed that seat because he had a tendency to get “airsick.” I later realized that he must’ve taken flights on this plane before and knew which seek to ask for. The second row of two seats was comfortable, but if you are tall (6 feet) your window is down and behind you. You do have access to see what’s going on through the front windows, but since there is a single propeller, the propeller artifact will be captured in all of your still and video footage. The people in the seats behind the second row seem to be trying to look out our windows so I must assume that their vision was limited too. In the future I would not fly a plane like this without being able to specifically handpick my seat. They had larger planes which seemed to offer individual windows for each passenger, but I assume since there were only five people taking the trip they chose not to take one. That may be the problem with signing up for a flight in advance and paying in advance – you don’t have much control over what plane they choose.  The pilot was great – he made it really easy with a very smooth takeoff, landing, and ride. In the future though I would not reserve a flight without knowing exactly what kind of plane I was going in, what kind of window access I had for photos and video, and see whether or not the propeller would be creating artifacts as well. Apparently we are told that you can only actually get to the top of Denali perhaps one third of the time no matter what type of flight you have signed up for. We had signed up for the Denali flyover and landing on a glacier, but wisely they declined as the weather did not permit it. We did get the proper refund since we had paid for the more expensive trip in advance.  Again, I have the highest regard both for the company and the pilot my complaint is that the plane they chose did not permit me to accomplish what I had wanted to do on the trip – not only see things but take pictures and video as well.  The reason for giving it only 2 stars is that for the price I expected not only to have an interesting flight but have good vision and be easily able to take pictures and video as well. I therefore was disappointed.

Nel nostro soggiorno a Talkeetna abbiamo voluto prendere il K2AVIATION nonostante il tempo non permetteva di avvicinarsi alla montagna Mt McKinley e non avendo più giorni per aspettare le condizioni meteo favorevoli siamo saltati a bordo per un volo di battesimo sui piccoli aerei turistici in attesa del volo previsto ad Homer per il bear adventure... Abbiamo sorvolato la foresta ed una miriade di fiumi ad un prezzo ridotto ($90). Ci hanno fatto pesare prima per questioni di sicurezza e ci hanno dato tutte le informazioni sul volo che mi ha tranquillizzato. Esperienza positiva grazie al personale competente ed efficiente. Ma vale la pena solo se si è così fortunati da poter volare sulla montagna che sembra accada solo al 30% dei visitatori!....
----
During our stay in Talkeetna we decide to take a flight with K2AVIATION, even if it was too cloudy to see the famous Mt. McKinley; it seems that only 30% of visitors get to see the mountain!!!…. They emphasized safety, made us weigh in for the plane loading and explained everything necessary for a safe flight. So we felt pretty secure and got our first flight in a small private plane, for a special low price, over the town and the surrounding rivers and forest. It was a great adventure, the pilot talked about the area we were seeing but I still feel sorry about missing the great mountain… Next time!

Review Title: Absolutely the very best part of our Alaska trip!
Review Text: You absolutely cannot visit Alaska and Denali National Park without taking a flightseeing tour -- and K2 is the BEST, bar none.  We talked to many others in the area and everyone raves about them because they specialize in the tour experience, not just ferrying climbers (though they are popular for doing that too).  The pilot who gave our tour was not only a skilled aviator but also extremely knowledgeable about the history and science of the area, telling great stories and pointing out fascinating points of interest through the pilot headsets we all wore. Takeoff and landing was smooth and we never felt nervous or airsick at all -- such a lovely flight!  The office staff was so friendly and helpful, and extremely flexible if you need to reschedule your tour due to weather as we did -- we found out that the summit of Mt. McKinley is only visible 30% of the time due to weather, but they are great about offering other options or rescheduling your flight, etc. And the aircraft is gorgeous, spotlessly maintained and comfortable. Even if you don't see the summit there is SO MUCH incredible stuff to see in the park on your flight.  There are things we saw on this tour that very few people will ever see and that will take your breath away -- 35-mile-long glaciers, sheer cliff amphitheaters, passes so dramatic it feels like your wingtips will scrape the sides (they're not even close, but it feels that way!), the Great Gorge that's deeper than the Grand Canyon, glacial pools that are literally Windex blue, ice crevasses and ice falls, on and on.  Of course if the weather is nice as it was for us, you'll see Mt McKinley (Denali), the highest summit in North America and and the rest of the range (Foraker-Denali's Wife and Hunter-Denali's child) and probably ask yourself who would be crazy enough to climb those things (a thousand try every spring, and less than half make it!).  Even my teenage kids were speechless and taking photos nonstop -- if you're a photographer you better bring an extra memory card!  And the optional glacier landing is a MUST -- we will never forget landing on skis and walking around on an actual glacier in the shadow of the most dramatic mountain scenery anywhere.  This is a trip of just a few hours that we will NEVER, never forget. Worth every penny and more!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: This summer I was able to experience the K2 aviation staff, service, safety, and their desire to provide an excellent adventure.  The office was a pleasant experience as we checked in with good conversation about our upcoming flight which built on to the excitement.  There was great emphasis on safety as they made us weigh in for the plane loading and the pilot (Scott) explained everything necessary for a safe flight right as we stood around the plane.  I was impressed that this was a priority as I just expected to get on a plane and go.  The plane was very clean on the outside and inside which added to the assurance that K2 took care of their equipment meticulously.  We also were given a lot of information about the plane itself, when it was made, etc. which we all found interesting.  So before we even started the flight we felt safe and had a little history lesson.  The flight itself was absolutely amazing.  Our pilot gave us a ton of information as we watched in awe at the size of the rivers and mountains, the colors of the glaciers and glacier water, and marveled at the muskeg and forest in the area.  We flew through a  pass that had sheer cliffs on both sides which made me think of how small the mountains in my home state of Wyoming are compared to the Alaskan landscape.  We landed on a glacier which was really exciting and something that I will never forget.  We had a lot of time to take pictures and talk about the surrounding mountains and features which was great.  It wasn't just a land, take a pic, and leave type of thing.  We took a different route back to the airport than what we took on the way up to the glacier.  That was nice because we saw twice the country.  We saw a black bear that was dark as night on the return and learned that you can see moose and Dall sheep also.  The kids absolutely loved every single second of the experience.  If you are planning a flight tour you should not chance any service other than K2.  K2 is excellent in service, safety, and the experience.  Choose K2 and you won't be disappointed.

Review Title: Awesome flight, even more awesome staff and crew
Review Text: We booked our McKinley Experience tour months before our vacation and planned a 3 day stay in Talkeetna.  The day of our arrival, it was raining, although K2 was still running flights.  They gave us the option of postponing for better weather (it was our first day in town) or going for it.  Originally, we decided to go for it.  We got into the plane (just us and the pilot) and made it all the way to the runway, when another pilot already out in the park called in to say that the visibility was worse due to low clouds.  Our pilot stopped the plane and gave us the option of coming back another day - this time we took them up on it.  We got back to the office and they advised us that Saturday's weather forecast was much better, and they were more than happy to reschedule us for that day.  Turned out to be a spectacular day.  We were with another couple this time, but we all had window seats and the views were out of this world.  Our pilot (wish I could remember his name) was wonderful - pointed out all the various mountains and points of interest.  The flight was very smooth and I never once felt sick (I'm not the greatest flyer).  I'd do it again in a heartbeat.  These people are truly professionals and care very much about providing a great experience.  Would definitely recommend.  In fact, I'd say it's a "must do" while in Alaska!

Review Text:
Before my Princess Inside Passage Cruise I booked a flight for four around McKinley with K2. I told them specifically where I was staying and was told they provided transport to/ from my lodging to their facility.

Upon arriving in Talkeetna, the day before our flight with my wife, 83 year old father in law, and his 79 year old friend , I stopped into the K2 office to confirm our appointment and pick up. The weather was very rainy with a forecast for more rain and high wind on our flight day. They assure me all was confirmed and that they would pick us up half an hour before our scheduled time to fly.
When leaving Talkeetna by Princess bus to our accommodations ,I discovered we were staying about an hour away from K2, and became concerned about our pick up time for our flight the next morning. I again contacted K2 again to confirm a time. This time I mention my concern for the timing of their pickup and my distance away from them.
This time, however , K2 told me they only do pick ups within ten minutes of their facility and it was my responsibility to get all four people to their office by eight am.
I asked for k2 to call us to let us know if the flight would occur to save us the expense ($10 each) and hassle of a early morning hour long shuttle ride. They said we needed to physically be in their facility by 8 am....and we're unwavering .
My understanding was that if we did not show our fee would be forfit regardless of the weather.

When we all showed up at 8 am , in pouring rain, they canceled our epic flight and offered a flight of the town instead , at the same price. We were not interested in this and so they refunded our fee. The atmosphere in the office was sullen and quite.

I'm a fairly easy going person but non the less found the staff at K2 to be unfriendly , unhelpful, and unconcerned with
My needs as a customer. We talked to friends in our tour group who had booked with other groups and had much clearer and better service.
After our canceled flight we went to the Roadhouse for breakfast and coffee to warm our bones and were thrilled by the friendly staff there.

Review Title: K2, No better way to see Denali!
Review Text:
No matter how many bus trips you take or walking tours or ranger presentations you experience, you will never fully grasp the grandeur, the beauty, the breath-taking topography of Denali, until you fly up to the mountain with K2. You will not even scratch the surface of what is there to be seen. The nearest road is miles away, and it would take you weeks to hike in, and then you would only see a very small portion of the mountain.
K2's outstanding bush pilots know every part of the mountain and will show you things you only read about like the "10,000 Foot Camp", the "West Butress", or "The Moose's Tooth".
They have a trip for every level of adventurer and every budget.
Bring your camera, there is no better way to see Alaska. This will be the highlight of your trip, the one thing you will remember always about your time in Alaska.

Review Text:
You know fickle Alaska weather can be. Out flight-seeing trip (with glacier landing) was postponed 3 times before we were able to make the trip. After being cursed by bad weather, low clouds, and poor visibility for 3 days, my wife and I rescheduled one final time for first flight out of the morning we were supposed to leave Talkeetna. When we woke up, the entire area was blanketed in fog so we went back to bed. The a peek of blue sky appeared through the window and when I looked out...wham the sky was clearing fast.

We scarfed down breakfast, loaded the car and headed to the airport to see if we could make the flight. By the time we reached the airport, the fog was gone and there wasn't a cloud in the sky.

The flight went off as planned and we were in the first aircraft to land on the glacier that morning. The upper level winds were calm which permitted flight close to the snow-covered sheer mountain walls...what a sight to behold!

This tops one of the best adventures I've ever had and I highly recommend K2. Everyone was great, informative, and professional.

Mt. Foraker, Mt. Hunter, Mt. Silverthrone, Harper Glacier from the top, Kahitna Glacier,

Review Title: Did their best to give us a good experience
Review Text: We had signed up and paid for the Denali Grand Tour with a glacier landing months in advance. I spoke by phone with K2 personnel who answered all my questions about their flight seeing trips and who explained that the trip we would actually get (especially the glacier landing) was dependent upon weather conditions the day of the scheduled flight - and these conditions could vary quickly.  When we arrived at K2's office in Talkeetna for our 11:00 tour, it was overcast with sporadic rain, and we were informed there would be no glacier landings that day - and the Grand Tour we had planned would have to be cut to a lower-level glacier tour.  As flights already in the air returned, the K2 people used the up-to-the-minute information provided by the pilots, as well as continuous monitoring of weather conditions, to decide exactly which trip they could offer us.  Our trip ended up leaving about 1/2 hour late, on a trial basis to see how far we could get - not very far, as it turned out, because fog started to encroach on the runway we would land on.  This 20-minute flight over the bogs at the foot of the glacier was free; we could abandon our flight seeing plans at that point with a full refund, or wait around to see if conditions would improve enough for a second try.  After an hour or so they did - and pilot Chris took us up again, showing us the Ruth Glacier and other ice fields, though he was unable to bring us into the "amphitheater" that is supposed to be most spectacular.  K2 promised to refund us for the tour portions it was unable to offer us. I was very impressed with K2's emphasis on safety and its efforts to accommodate our desire for a good experience within the possibilities that could be attempted safely.  They were flexible, offering us the alternative of taking another flight, at higher altitude, during which we would overfly no glaciers but might get to see Mount McKinley. We decided we would rather take a flight where we would definitely see SOMETHING, even if it wasn't the mountain.  Our time waiting in the K2 office was fairly pleasant. Their waiting area is quite comfortable, with free coffee. We left feeling satisfied despite the uncooperative weather.

Review Text: This company is the absolute best to fly McKinley (Denali) with.  Don't bother with your cruise booking.  Its always a dice roll whether McKinley will be "out" or what the weather will be but they handled it better than any expectations.  They met us at Grand Denali Lodge (where we were on a pre-cruise tour).  Immediately we were told the weather was not suitable for our 1:00PM time and we were offered a refund or a rebooking later in the day.  We chose to be transported to their office which was extremely busy, but very organized.  We chose to rebook for the next available, now at 5:00PM.  They would have returned us to the hotel but we chose to wander around town and take the shuttle back.  At 4:20PM we called them and the flight was on.  They picked us up again at 4:30PM and off we went, taking off at 5:00PM.  As we went above the clouds with our pilot (34 years experience)  the mountain was out.  The rest of the flight was unbelievable.  It felt as though we could touch the sheer walls at one point.  We were to have a glacier landing but the designated area was too foggy so that did not occur.  Although a bit of a disappointment at the time it did not take away from the trip.  On return to the office we asked how much was still due as we had prepaid 50%.  Immediately, without any prompting, we were told the price was reduced for no glacier landing and reduced flight time due to no landing.  What service!  The flight was superb, but we were also lucky the mountain showed, and the service was exemplary.  One suggestion:  book as early in the day as possible so you can rebook later in the day if needed (remember it doesn't get dark until about 11:00 PM).  What memories!!!

Review Title: Glacier landing was the highlight of our trip!
Review Text: We didn't know what to expect during our flight near Mt. McKinley.  We thought flying in a 6-seater plane might make us airsick and told our pilot about our extended bout of motion sickness on a boat tour of Kenai Fjords National Park.  He reassured us that we would be fine.  We had agreed to a glacier landing on Ruth Glacier and it was a fantastic experience!  The only things we needed were jacket, sunglasses, walking/hiking shoes and camera.  Our personal belongings were left in a locked bin at the office.  Our pilot, who had made the trip thousands of times, took us up 5000 feet smoothly, and it was very peaceful flying close to the mountains.  The glacier landing was similar to landing on deep snow.  We got out of the plane and were delighted to be stomping around on a glacier.  An amazing sight was a couple who were sitting on the glacier like they were at the beach.  The couple told us they had rented a house up there for a couple of days and had flown up with K2.  By the way, after the flight we learned that pilot Doug Geeting is also a musician who performs locally.  Unfortunately, we weren't around to catch his act.  We are so glad we made the glacier landing!  Go if you have the opportunity.

Review Text:
We were traveling in Alaska for about 1.5 weeks in September of 2011. We knew that we would have to be flexible with the weather but we were hopeful things would work out. At the start of the trip we had to cancel some water events on the coast due to rain and wind. We had a chance to visit the Denali state park and had a great time on the Tundra Wilderness Tour. We had not gotten a view of Mt. McKinley but also understood that only 30% of people get to see the mountain so we enjoyed our visit in the park and the animals that got to see. Heading south to Talkeetna we were amazed to see the clouds clear up and Mount McKinley finally show. We had a flight schedule with K2 Aviation the next morning but we knew that by then it might be back in the clouds. We gave K2 Aviation a call and they were very helpful in letting us move our trip time.

They came to pick us up at the hotel and we found that four others were also scheduled for next day and moved their time. As we now had a total of seven people going they sent us up in a twin prop plane. The plane was in great shape and comfortable. We took off and had the just the best flight. The pilot gave us some great narrative on the mountain and what we were seeing. The air was so smooth and the plan really quick. We were at the mountain within 15 minutes and flew around the mountain for at least 35 minutes. No matter which way you looked it was just amazing. I consider this one of the best events of the trip. If you are in the area and the weather breaks you really need to look K2 Aviation up and take a flight with them. The memories will last a lifetime.

Review Title: Grand Denali with glacier landing - What a view!
Review Text:
Second visit to Alaska hoping to see Mt McKinley in it's full glory and I was lucky. Waking to a beautiful sunrise on Mt McKinley I arranged with the tour desk at Talkeetna Lodge to take a Grand Denali Tour with glacier landing (2hr tour) with K2 aviation on the 3pm flight.

K2 aviation shuttle picked up 1/2hr prior to scheduled flight and returned to the lodge. Any clients with a glacier landing are offered overboots free of charge to cover their joggers or other light shoes. The Grand Denali tour with glacier landing had 10 passengers and so used a DeHaviland Otter with the pilot giving a safety talk and procedures for glacier walk prior to boarding. We were advised there may be some turbulence due to warm air over the mountains but we never had any. Seating was first in with a single seat at every window ensuring everyone had a stunning view, the back seat was low slung so I felt was really only suitable for tall people as you had to lean a little forward to see out the windows and one passenger was accommodated in the co-pilot seat. As an enthusiastic photographer I sat in the seat opposite the door and the downside was many images had the wing strut and wing tip in the left side of the photo. However, I was able to overcome this by using 'Live view' on my camera and pointing the lens backwards. Probably would be better to try and get into the forward seats. It didn't matter which side you sat as the pilot and route allowed spectacular views from both. The landing onto Ruth Glacier was smooth and the 1/2hr was long enough to take photos of other planes arriving/departing and the surrounding mountains. It also allows you to appreciate the depth of the snow.

I initially wanted the summit flight but was hesitant and decided on this as the day was glorious and we saw the summit along with numerous other mountains in the Alaskan range. The return flight and landing was excellent better than some commercial flights. Well worth the expense for the grandeur and appreciation of the mountain climbers tenacity and stamina. If you have taken the time to get to Talkeetna/Denali and the mountain is out spend the money for one of the highlights of Alaksa, it's the icing on top of the cake.

Review Title: for those visiting on a time budget--just be aware to have a plan B
Review Text: I specifically booked on K2 for their reviews. Flew 7+hrs from houston to anchorage and this was supposed to be my highlight for my trip. i was booked with K2 for sat 9/3 for a tour+landing (they charge 1/2 on your CC and rest when you show up). Before leaving Anchorage called them at 803am that day to verify landing and the lady on the phone said "yes, we're landing this morning". Drove the slightly over 2 hours to talkeetna and during checkin at 1015am, the gentleman that was there (tall slim guy) mentioned they would fly for the tour but <1% chance of landing. When asked about other landings told to me on the phone, they said they never even landed that morning due to weather and also that its bad to land in the summer time. Clearly this was an expectation bummer to me from the first call that am to the reality check at the counter since i'm one of those that hate surprises. All they had to do was tell me the same on the phone that chances were looking slim to land today and that would have been more than enough warning to me to be atleast have planned for plan B incase this did not work. I asked for why the discrepancy over the phone with what the lady said just 2hrs ago vs. now at the counter and got absolutely NO apology for that. Yes, i did get my refund but again my point is for those on a time crunch since i visited alaksa for just the labor day weekend, beware that even if you do not get to land (if thats what you want, like i did) you may be still told on the phone to come in. (i wish that same gentleman i spoke to in person had answered the phone that morning saving me this review. It would'nt have been frustrating at all, had both the messages on the phone+in person were in sync). But obvisouly keeping safety in mind, it was best to not land (i'm just a little frustrated that the same could have been communicated over the phone to either help a customer avoid the road trip or have a plan B to do in talkeetna---that's all). The actual problem is as with any airline making $ from tourists, they would NOT like to say NO on the phone to any customer and K2 is no exception. Just be careful for those on a time budget, pls. try to check prior to your roadtrip as best you can since they do offer re-scheduling or atleast keep something else in talkeetna to do as plan B (which is what i did in the end taking the rapids cruise on the talkeetna river. i was lucky to find this on the spot there but i would suggest you plan for a plan B).

Review Title: Trip of a lifetime-You must do this!
Review Text: I have to admit I was not looking forward to this trip, being a plane wimp, but this plane adventure was truly awesome!  The day we had scheduled was cold and rainy with very little visibility, but K2 rescheduled without any hesitation for later that week when the weather looked better.  This was our very last day in Alaska, so we were praying for the clouds to part, which they did.  Our pilot, Barry, was a fellow Hoosier and was a medvac in the past, which relaxed me a little.  It was just our family in the small plane and I sat in the back for photography reasons (he said) probably had to do more with weight distribution.  I was gearing myself up for a bumpy scary ride, but it never happened.  From the time we took off until we landed it was smooth, relaxing and spectacular.  Barry was very informative about the plane itself, the scenery and the glaciers, plus interesting humorous stories of past flights.  After the initial few seconds, I really wasn't scared at all, even with the glacier landing, which was a blast.  SOOOOO cool standing on a real glacier in the mountains of Alaska.  My two teenagers absolutely loved the trip also. Very few people get to even see Mount Denali, let alone fly around it and land on a glacier.  This was by far our favorite part of our two week vacation, and we had a great vacation.  It is expensive I not going to lie about that, but so worth every penny!!  Buy a Tour Saver coupon book and you can get a two for one offer.  Thanks so much, Barry!!  Have fun with those grandkids!!

Review Text:
We flew with Chuck West as the pilot in Cessna 185. I was with my wife. The two other passengers were two women, probably friends.
We expected a standard sightseeing flight. To our delight, the pilot was also expalining the landscape on our way to and from Mount Denali. I hold a private pilot licence since 30 years and have a university formation in physical geography, so I could apprciate the flying skills and the geographical knowledge of Mr West. This was my first experience in mountain flying. Usually my wife does not like flying because she is prone to motion sickness. But she felt all right for the hole flight (1½ hour). In addition to geographic comments, Mr West was constantly explaining his manoeuvres and reassuring the passengers especially when apparently flying close to summits and explaining that things are farther than they appear. I have worked for 25 years on helicopters in the Air Force and experienced many interesting flights, but this one was THE flight of my life and for my wife as well.
I could also appreciate the kindness of other personnel. The young woman at the desk offered us a ride to the bus stop altough it was only a 2 minute walk. Further more, I forgot something in the aircraft. The day after the flight I telephoned to K2 and Michael (if I remember well) arranged thing so diligently that this item was sent to the company's office I was travelling with in time before I embarked on the train. Thank you very much by the way.
Being the smallest guy I had to be in the back seat which is the best place for filming and photos.
My wife and me highly recommend K2 Aviation. Surely all the pilots there show great professionalism, but I can tell you if you fly with Chuck West you will have a great flight.

Robert Frenette
Québec, Canada

Review Title: Incredible Scenery, only exceeded by the professional service of K2.
Review Text:
Our Flight Seeing adventure with K2 Aviation in Talkeetna, AK was the highlight of our 10 day Alaskan vacation. Although we traveled to several other cities and participated in many other attractions, our Flight Seeing trip with K2 was by far the highlight of our family vacation. The K2 employees were all personable, professional and welcoming from the gentleman fueling the planes, to the office staff who attended to every detail for our party to be sure we were prepared properly for our chosen flight. Selecting a flight was no easy task with all K2 had to offer, but after discussions with Trevor the very well informed Flight Scheduler we selected the Glacier Lake landing on a Dehaviland Beaver Float Plane.
Our pilot Randy not only made my entire family feel safe and secure from the push off from the dock until our splash down back at Fish Lake the lake of departure. Randy's informative and humorous conversation quickly put anxious nerves at ease during the flight, taking time to point out interesting landmarks and educate us about the geologic formations and glacier dynamics. His information turned this outing into as much a learning experience as it was an exciting family adventure. After gliding deep into gorgeous mountain valleys above sky blue glaciers with glacier melt carving deep ravines forming frigid glacial rivers, we landed on a remote glacial lake deep in the heart of the glaciers. Once we landed and the plane was secured, we disembarked and were introduced to two friendly professional and informative guides that continued to educate us to the beauty and unique features this area offers. As we hiked up mountain paths the local wildlife and fauna was pointed out and discussed. Flowing mountain streams were crossed and gorgeous photo ops abounded in a part of the world few human's feet ever get the chance to travel.
At the completion of our hike we were treated to delicious locally produced products such as cheeses, sausages and salmon and a few different selections of wine. It was a thoroughly well thought out excursion leaving nothing more we could ask for.
Upon our return to the float plane base on Fish Lake , I realized I had seen this picturesque location in a published photo somewhere in my past. I have attached my photo for you to compare.

It gets no better than this, thank you K2 for a full and wonderful Family Adventure!

Review Title: Fly with K2 and you will not be sorry! Thank You Greg Sanoski!!!!!!!!!!
Review Text:
My wife and I flew with K2 on July 17th and we had the time of our lives! As you may be aware of, In Alaska, there is no guaranteed view of the mountain with changing weather. This is why we opted to spend the bucks on a flight-seeing tour. I made reservations for the glacier landing but upon arriving found that it was considered unsafe because timing put us in the later part of the season and the landing area was getting slushy. There was no beating around the bush by Talkeetna. The desk attendant made the announcement that there would be no landings today and that a full refund would be given. Since they have done this thousands of times, I trusted their decision and went for the alternate anyway. that's why I made this Journey.

Our pilot was Greg Sanoski. He more than made up for the altered reservation. I'm sure all of the pilots at K2 are great, but Greg showed us the times of our lives. We were very lucky flying in from the East and got the most fantastic sunlit view of the top of Denali!!!! He circled around and between the clouds taking time to give great narration as we viewed the great corridor, Ruth Glacier, Sheldon Amphitheater and many more of his favorite spots. Review Title: K2 Aviation: "Wow" Is All We Can Say!
Review Text:
All I can say is GO. And K2 is the company to GO with.
That's our experience. And what an experience it was...

If you have the means and the wherewithall to
afford this trip, it is worth every penny and K2
is the company to fly with. The trip is expensive for sure.
but what the heck... You only live once. You'll never have an experience
like this again. Denali at 20,000 feet. It is the grandest adventure beyond your wildest
dreams.

I don't have the luxury of comparing K2 Aviation with other
flight comapnies in the area.

But I can share with you, this IS the trip of a liftetime,
an incredible memory that you will always remember.

We selected the two hour Denali Grand Tour, and believe me, it was
worth it.

The K2 Staff is incredibly relaxed, courteous, and well organized.
They are certainly willing to spend time with you via email, over the phone,
or in person answering all your questions and addressing your concerns.
They are a great crew.

We traveled with them on Wednesday June 8, at 1PM. Tony was our pilot.
There were a lot of people flying that day at different times.

The weather in Alaska is tricky and constantly changing. The weather on Denali
even more so, as the mountain makes it's own weather. The pilots and the company itself, are very attuned to the constantly changing weather conditions. If in doubt, they simply won't fly. Period. The safety of their customers has the highest importance.

There had been rain in the area for several days prior to our trip, and the day we flew,
it was partly sunny with some low lying clouds. So weather was a possible concern.

We took off right on time. Once we got above the clouds our views were unimpeded and they were just stunning. Words simply cannot describe the jaw dropping majesty of this flight. You'd have to see our photos and High Definition videos to comprehend this.

The Glacier landing was spectacular! At that elevation the sun was very strong. The air was cold, but not terribly so. Would suggest bringing gloves and some good sunblock.

Tony, our pilot, carefully watched an ominous low hanging cloud just over the peak. He stated that if he gave the signal, we had to board immediately and make a hasty retreat, adding to the drama of the trip. But that ominous cloud never brought any dramatic, sudden weather changes to our location. We spent probably 20-25 minutes on the Glacier and took tons of photos. It was incredible.

The return trip back to base was beautiful. The flight, smooth all the way, and not rushed.
Tony's narration throughout the flight was very complete and informative.

Yes, this is expensive. But you'll never have an opportunity like this again.

We loved our K2 experience!

I highly recommend this professional company.

Review Text:
This was our first trip to Alaska. We really had no plans other than hanging out with our grand children, daughter, and son-in-law and visit a friend’s home in Cooper Landing.

Our daughter surprised us with a K2 flight seeing tour of Mt. McKinley. We were thinking OK up and around the mountain and back to the air strip. But that was not the program. We actually toured the surrounding area including all mountains and learned the history of the area. We saw Mt. McKinley from every direction and then we landed on the mountain. Words cannot express the breathtaking beauty of it all and the hush of the mountain.

This is truly an adventure that each person has to experience at least once in their lifetime. Our K2 flight was the crème de la crème to a vacation that we have told everyone was the best ever.

Review Title: K2 Aviation, Talkeetna, Alaska - Fabulous experience!
Review Text: My husband and I just returned from a 2 week trip to Alaska and are now members of the 30% Club because we were one of the fortunate few who got to see Mt. McKinley in all its glory.  Because of this good fortune, we decided at the last minute to take a flight tour with K2 Aviation.  We were part of a Princess Cruisetour and the staff at McKinley Lodge assisted with the booking of the plane ride.  Upon our arrival at K2 Aviation we were greeted by friendly desk staff.  The 1-1/4 hour McKinley Flyer trip was absolutely fabulous!  Our experienced pilot, Jeff, was outstanding and made me, a reluctant small plane passenger, immediately comfortable.  The flight was incredibly smooth and the scenery unbelievable.  My husband and I must have taken well over 100 photos during the ride.  Next time we'll definitely do a glacier landing.  We would highly recommend this company which is run by the well-known Rust family as well worth your money and time.

Review Text: This was such a neat experience! There are a variety of sizes of planes and not to worry, you won't get sick! The pilots are well trained and make the flight as smooth as possible. They fly you right up next to and in and out of the mountains. It is really neat and I would definitely recommend doing this if you go to Alaska. There is no better way to see the land!

Review Text: My family and I went on the 1.5 hour Denali flightseeing trip last week with a  pilot named Randy. He flew us up in a Cessna that was just right for all four of us. He was really great and showed us the beauty of Denali, up close and personal. We saw the base camp for all of the climbers that scale the mountain and the massive glaciers and mountains of the Alaska range. The Ruth Amphitheater and the great Gorge of the Ruth Glacier were just two of the many highlights. My mom couldn't talk about it because she was too busy actually crying at the beauty of it all. Don't miss this trip, it's the experience of a lifetime.

Review Title: We were another group that had planned to...
Review Text:
We were another group that had planned to fly on August 12th, but conditions were bad and worsening as our flightsee time approached. The office staff were extremely helpful and accomodating, offering us the choice of taking one of their non-Denali trips with a refund of the price difference or waiting a day to see if conditions improved. We chose to postpone our trip for a day and are very glad that we did.

Friday the 13th actually proved to be a fantastic day. The weather cleared up and Denali "came out", showing itself and allowing us to take the tour we signed up for. We also got the added treat of a glacier landing, which we had been told the day before was likely out of the question for the remainder of the season. All in all, I highly recommend K2 Aviation.

Review Text: In June 2010 4 of us took the Grand Denali Tour.  Booking this tour on our own separate from the cruise line was a bit tricky but saved us a great deal.  Elaine from K2 was most pleasant & helpful.  The flight left right on time & we were fortunate enough to have the plane, a 4 seater to ourselves.  The pilot, Randy was excellent, very detailed & thoughtful . . .so much so that numerous times he would bank the plane so I could take better pictures.  Randy was also very informative in telling us what we were viewing at any given time.  While this was our first & only flightseeing experience in Alaska I cannot imagine how any operator could top K2!  Highly recommended!

Review Text: Our K2 flight was a great way to see the mountain "up close".  Taking off from Talkeetna and heading towards the mountain, our pilot explained the geology of the area, pointed out the interesting sites, and soon we were climbing over glaciers and heading up Mt McKinley.  At some points, flying between 2 rock faces several thousand feet high, it seemed the wingtips were close enough to touch the rocks, though our pilot did let us know we had hundreds of feet of clearance.  The sights were amazing, and the landing on the glacier very much worth the extra charge.  K2 was professional all the way, the pilot did a great job of keeping up a running commentary and answering questions (and, of course, flying the plane), and I highly recommend the trip to anyone visiting the area.
